title: Set up the initial application infrastructure.
description:
Create the initial project structure for the React frontend, Spring Boot REST API and PostgreSQL database. Configure containerized local development using Docker Compose, environment-specific configuration, database connection management and health-check endpoints. Establish a consistent project structure so developers can work on the frontend and backend independently.
Acceptance criteria:
- The frontend, backend and PostgreSQL database can be started using the documented container commands.
- The frontend can communicate with the backend through the configured API base URL.
- The backend connects to PostgreSQL using environment variables rather than hardcoded credentials.
- Database migrations run automatically or through a documented command.
- The backend exposes a health-check endpoint that verifies application and database availability.
- Environment secrets are excluded from source control.

title: Sign in using the university SSO.
description:
As a university student, professor or staff member, I want to sign in using the university's single sign-on service, so that I can access RoomBook with my institutional account without creating another password.
Acceptance criteria:
- Given an unauthenticated user, when they select Sign in, then they are redirected to the university SSO authentication page.
- Given successful authentication, when the SSO service returns a valid response, then RoomBook creates an authenticated session and redirects the user to the application.
- Given unsuccessful authentication, when the SSO service rejects the credentials, then the user receives an appropriate error message and remains unauthenticated.
- The backend validates the SSO response before granting access.
- Authentication tokens and session credentials are not exposed in frontend logs or URLs after the callback is processed.
- The application displays an appropriate message when the SSO service is temporarily unavailable.

title: Sign out of RoomBook securely.
description:
As an authenticated user, I want to sign out of RoomBook, so that other people using the same device cannot access my account.
Acceptance criteria:
- An authenticated user can access a Sign out action from the application navigation.
- When the user signs out, the application invalidates its active session.
- The user is redirected to the public sign-in page after signing out.
- Attempting to access a protected page after signing out redirects the user to authentication.
- The application does not retain access to protected data through browser navigation after logout.

title: The application retains an active session after sign out.
description:
When a user selects Sign out, the frontend redirects to the login page, but the backend session remains valid. As a result, the user can access protected API endpoints using the previously issued session credentials. The expected behavior is for the backend to invalidate the session and reject subsequent authenticated requests.
Reproduction steps:
1. Sign in through the university SSO.
2. Open a protected page or capture an authenticated API request.
3. Select Sign out.
4. Repeat the previously authenticated API request.
Expected result: the request is rejected because the session has been invalidated.
Actual result: the API still accepts the session credentials.
Acceptance criteria:
- The logout operation invalidates the server-side session.
- Previously issued session credentials cannot access protected endpoints after logout.
- The frontend clears authentication-related session data.
- A regression test verifies that authenticated requests fail after logout.

title: View institutional profile information.
description:
As an authenticated university user, I want to view my RoomBook profile and institutional information, so that I can verify which account is being used to make booking requests.
Acceptance criteria:
- The profile page displays the user's full name and institutional e-mail address obtained from the authenticated identity.
- The page displays the user's institutional identifier when it is provided by the SSO service.
- The page displays the user's assigned RoomBook roles.
- Profile information is retrieved from the authenticated account rather than submitted as arbitrary frontend data.
- A user cannot view another user's private profile information through the profile endpoint.

title: Manage mappings between institutional groups and RoomBook roles.
description:
As a RoomBook administrator, I want to associate university identity groups with application roles, so that students, professors, staff members and administrative personnel receive the appropriate permissions automatically.
Acceptance criteria:
- Administrators can view the institutional groups configured for RoomBook.
- Administrators can associate an institutional group with one or more supported RoomBook roles.
- Supported roles include student, professor, staff member, booking approver and system administrator.
- The application resolves a user's RoomBook permissions from the validated SSO group information and configured mappings.
- A user without a recognized group receives only the permissions explicitly allowed for unassigned accounts.
- Only users with the system administrator permission can modify role mappings.
- Changes to role mappings are persisted and applied to subsequent authorization checks.

title: Removed institutional roles remain active in existing sessions.
description:
When an administrator removes a user's institutional group from a role mapping, the user may continue accessing features associated with the previous role through an existing session. The expected behavior is for authorization to reflect the current role mappings according to the application's session and permission refresh policy.
Reproduction steps:
1. Sign in as a user belonging to an institutional group mapped to the booking approver role.
2. Keep the user's session active.
3. Sign in as a system administrator and remove that group from the booking approver mapping.
4. Attempt to access an approver-only endpoint using the original session.
Expected result: the user no longer has the removed permission after the configured authorization refresh.
Actual result: the previous permission remains effective.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorization checks use the current effective role assignments.
- Changes to role mappings invalidate or refresh affected permissions according to the implemented session policy.
- A user without the approver permission cannot access approver-only frontend routes or backend endpoints.
- Automated tests cover role removal while a session is active.

title: Browse the university resource catalog.
description:
As a university user, I want to browse a catalog of available rooms, laboratories and equipment, so that I can discover resources that I may request.
Acceptance criteria:
- The catalog displays resources marked as active and published.
- Each resource entry displays its name, resource type and location.
- Resource types distinguish rooms, laboratories and equipment.
- Resources marked as inactive or unpublished are not displayed to ordinary users.
- The catalog retrieves its information through a paginated REST API endpoint.
- An appropriate empty state is displayed when no resources are available.

title: View the complete details of a resource.
description:
As a university user, I want to open a resource's detail page, so that I can evaluate its facilities and restrictions before submitting a booking request.
Acceptance criteria:
- The detail page displays the resource name, description, type and location.
- Room and laboratory details include capacity and available facilities when configured.
- Equipment details include identification information and relevant specifications when configured.
- The page displays access restrictions and resource operating hours when available.
- The resource's current publication status is respected when accessing its detail URL directly.
- The detail endpoint returns a not-found response for an unknown resource identifier.

title: Filter resources using catalog criteria.
description:
As a university user, I want to filter the resource catalog by resource type, campus, building and minimum capacity, so that I can find resources that match my booking requirements.
Acceptance criteria:
- The catalog provides filters for resource type, campus, building and minimum capacity where applicable.
- Users can combine multiple filter criteria in a single search.
- The backend applies all selected filters to the same result set.
- Changing or clearing a filter updates the displayed results.
- Selected filters remain visible while the user navigates between catalog pages.
- The system displays a clear message when no resources match the selected criteria.

title: Combined resource filters return incorrect results.
description:
When a user selects multiple catalog filters, the API may return resources matching only one of the selected criteria instead of requiring all selected criteria to match. The expected behavior is to combine the active filters using the appropriate AND conditions.
Reproduction steps:
1. Open the resource catalog.
2. Select a campus and a resource type.
3. Select a building belonging to that campus.
4. Review the returned resources.
Expected result: every resource matches the selected campus, resource type and building.
Actual result: resources that do not match one or more selected criteria may appear in the results.
Acceptance criteria:
- The API returns only resources matching every active filter.
- Clearing one filter preserves the remaining filter conditions.
- Filter combinations are covered by backend integration tests.
- Result counts and pagination reflect the filtered dataset.

title: Sort the resource catalog.
description:
As a university user, I want to sort catalog results by resource name or capacity, so that I can compare resources in an order that is useful for my search.
Acceptance criteria:
- Users can sort results by resource name in ascending or descending order.
- Room and laboratory results can also be sorted by capacity when capacity is available.
- The selected sorting option is applied consistently across catalog pages.
- Sorting works together with the filters already available in the catalog.
- Resources without a capacity value are handled consistently and do not cause API errors.
- The default ordering is documented and applied when no sorting option is selected.

title: View resource availability on a calendar.
description:
As a university user, I want to view a resource's availability on a calendar, so that I can identify suitable dates and time periods before requesting a booking.
Acceptance criteria:
- The resource detail page provides access to its availability calendar.
- Users can navigate between days and weeks.
- The calendar distinguishes available periods, approved bookings and active administrative blocks.
- Only information permitted for ordinary users is displayed about other users' bookings.
- Calendar events display their start and end times in the university's configured time zone.
- The calendar retrieves availability from the backend and reflects the resource's configured operating hours.

title: Calendar events crossing midnight appear on the wrong date.
description:
When a reservation or administrative block ends after midnight, the calendar may display the entire event on its start date or calculate its visible duration incorrectly. The expected behavior is to represent the event across all dates and time slots it occupies, using the university's configured time zone.
Reproduction steps:
1. Open the availability calendar for a resource.
2. Create or load an event starting before midnight and ending after midnight.
3. Navigate to both the starting date and the following date.
Expected result: the event is displayed across both dates with the correct start and end times.
Actual result: part or all of the event is displayed on the wrong date or omitted.
Acceptance criteria:
- Calendar rendering accounts for events spanning multiple calendar dates.
- Start and end timestamps are interpreted consistently using the configured time zone.
- Events are not duplicated as separate reservations in the backend.
- Automated tests cover events that start and end on different dates.

title: Submit a booking request for a room or laboratory.
description:
As a university student, professor or staff member, I want to request a room or laboratory for a specific date and time, so that I can use an appropriate university space for an academic or institutional activity.
Acceptance criteria:
- An authenticated user can start a booking request from a room or laboratory detail page.
- The request form identifies the selected resource and allows the user to specify a start date, end date, start time and end time.
- The user must provide a purpose for the requested booking.
- The user must provide the expected number of participants.
- The system validates that the end time is later than the start time.
- The system validates that the requested participant count does not exceed the configured resource capacity.
- A successful submission creates a request with an initial Pending status and a unique identifier.
- The requester can see a confirmation in the application after submission.

title: Submit a reservation request for standalone equipment.
description:
As a university user, I want to request equipment independently of a room booking, so that I can borrow university devices for academic or institutional activities.
Acceptance criteria:
- Users can initiate an equipment request from an equipment detail page.
- The form allows the requester to specify the requested equipment, quantity, pickup date and time, and expected return date and time.
- The system validates that the requested quantity does not exceed the configured available inventory.
- The requested pickup and return periods must follow the equipment's configured availability rules.
- The user must provide the intended use of the equipment.
- A successful request receives a unique identifier and Pending status.
- The request is associated with the authenticated requester.

title: Validate availability before accepting a booking request.
description:
As a university user, I want RoomBook to verify that the requested resource is available for the selected period, so that I do not submit requests that conflict with approved reservations or administrative blocks.
Acceptance criteria:
- The backend checks the resource's current availability when a request is submitted.
- A request overlapping an approved booking for the same resource is rejected.
- A request overlapping an active maintenance or event block is rejected.
- The conflict validation uses the full requested start and end timestamps.
- Requests for different resources can use overlapping periods without being treated as conflicting.
- The backend performs the availability validation as part of the submission operation rather than relying exclusively on previously displayed calendar data.
- When a conflict is detected, the request is not created and the user receives an explanatory message.

title: A booking request is accepted after its availability becomes outdated.
description:
A user can keep the booking form open after viewing an available period. If an administrator approves another request for the same resource and period before the first user submits the form, the first submission may still be accepted because the frontend uses outdated availability information. The expected behavior is to revalidate the requested period against current reservations and blocks when submitting.
Reproduction steps:
1. User A opens a resource calendar and selects an available period.
2. User A opens the booking form but does not submit it.
3. An administrator approves a conflicting request submitted by User B.
4. User A submits the previously opened booking form.
Expected result: the system rejects User A's request because the period is no longer available.
Actual result: User A's conflicting request is accepted.
Acceptance criteria:
- Availability is revalidated against current data at the time of submission.
- Concurrent submissions cannot create conflicting approved reservations through a race condition.
- The rejected submission does not create a booking request with an invalid reservation.
- The frontend informs the user that availability changed and asks them to select another period.
- Automated tests cover concurrent submissions and intervening approvals.

title: Track the status history of a booking request.
description:
As a requester, I want to view the status history of my booking request, so that I can understand how its evaluation has progressed and who performed each recorded action.
Acceptance criteria:
- The request detail page displays the current request status.
- The page displays each recorded status transition in chronological order.
- Each history entry includes the previous status, new status, date and time, and responsible user when applicable.
- Administrative comments associated with a transition are displayed to the requester when marked as visible to them.
- Requesters can access the history of their own requests.
- Users cannot access the private status history of requests belonging to other users unless they have the appropriate administrative permission.

title: Cancel a pending booking request.
description:
As a requester, I want to cancel one of my pending booking requests, so that the administrative office does not evaluate a request that I no longer need.
Acceptance criteria:
- A requester can cancel a booking request that belongs to their account and has Pending status.
- The system asks the requester to confirm the cancellation before applying it.
- A confirmed cancellation changes the request status to Cancelled.
- The cancellation is recorded in the request status history with the responsible user and timestamp.
- Requests that have already been approved, rejected or cancelled cannot be cancelled through this action.
- Users cannot cancel another user's request unless they have an explicit administrative permission.

title: Edit a pending booking request.
description:
As a requester, I want to update the details of my pending booking request, so that I can correct information or adjust my requirements before an administrator makes a decision.
Acceptance criteria:
- The requester can edit a request belonging to their account while its status is Pending.
- Editable information includes the purpose, participant count and requested date and time, subject to resource rules.
- Changes to the requested period trigger the same availability validation used during request submission.
- Changes that exceed the resource capacity are rejected with an explanatory message.
- Requests that are not Pending cannot be modified through this action.
- Each successful modification is recorded with the responsible user, timestamp and changed information.
- The request retains its original identifier and Pending status after a successful update.

title: Integrate RoomBook with the external e-mail service.
description:
Implement the backend integration responsible for sending transactional e-mails through the university-approved external e-mail service. Configure authentication, connection settings and sender identity through environment-specific secrets. Establish a reusable notification component so future features can send messages without implementing provider communication independently.
Acceptance criteria:
- The backend can authenticate with the configured e-mail provider using credentials stored outside source control.
- A reusable service exposes an operation for sending an e-mail to one or more recipients.
- The service supports recipient address, subject and message content.
- Provider responses and delivery errors are logged without exposing credentials or sensitive message content.
- Failed sending attempts are handled without causing the related booking transaction to be duplicated.
- Provider configuration can be changed between development, testing and production environments.
- An integration test verifies successful sending using the configured test environment or provider sandbox.

title: Receive an e-mail confirming booking request submission.
description:
As a requester, I want to receive an e-mail when I successfully submit a booking request, so that I have a record of the request and its identification details.
Acceptance criteria:
- A successful booking request submission triggers an e-mail to the requester's institutional e-mail address.
- The e-mail includes the request identifier, resource name, requested period and initial status.
- The e-mail clearly states that submission does not mean the booking has been approved.
- The message uses the configured RoomBook sender identity and notification template.
- An unsuccessful request submission does not trigger a confirmation e-mail.
- Failure to send the e-mail does not undo an otherwise successful request creation.
- The sending outcome is recorded for operational troubleshooting.

title: Retrying an e-mail delivery creates duplicate confirmation messages.
description:
When the external e-mail provider takes too long to respond, the notification component may retry a delivery that was already accepted by the provider. The requester then receives multiple confirmation messages for the same booking request. The expected behavior is to prevent duplicate notifications when the same delivery operation is retried.
Reproduction steps:
1. Configure a booking request that triggers the submission confirmation e-mail.
2. Simulate a provider response timeout after the provider has accepted the message.
3. Allow the notification component to retry the delivery operation.
4. Check the recipient's inbox.
Expected result: the requester receives only one confirmation message for the request.
Actual result: the requester receives duplicate confirmation messages.
Acceptance criteria:
- Notification deliveries have a unique identifier associated with the triggering event.
- Repeated processing of the same delivery identifier does not send another confirmation message when the first delivery was accepted.
- Provider responses are handled consistently for successful, failed and uncertain delivery outcomes.
- The notification delivery status can be inspected for troubleshooting.
- Automated tests cover provider timeouts and repeated delivery attempts.

title: View the administrative queue of pending booking requests.
description:
As a booking approver, I want to view a centralized queue of pending booking requests, so that I can identify which requests require administrative evaluation.
Acceptance criteria:
- Only users with the booking approver role can access the administrative request queue.
- The queue displays pending room, laboratory and equipment requests.
- Each entry displays the request identifier, requester, resource, requested period and submission date.
- Approvers can filter the queue by resource type, campus and submission date range.
- Approvers can sort requests by submission date and requested period.
- Selecting a queue entry opens its request details, including the information submitted by the requester.
- The queue supports pagination and displays the total number of matching pending requests.
- Requests cancelled by their owners are no longer displayed as pending.

title: Inspect the complete details of a booking request.
description:
As a booking approver, I want to inspect all information submitted with a booking request, so that I can make an informed administrative decision.
Acceptance criteria:
- The request detail page displays the request identifier, requester information, resource details, requested period, purpose and participant count or equipment quantity.
- The page displays the submission date and current status.
- Any additional information submitted by the requester is available to the approver.
- The page displays relevant resource restrictions and availability information for the requested period.
- Approvers can navigate from the request details back to the pending request queue.
- Users without the booking approver permission cannot access administrative request details.

title: Approve a pending booking request.
description:
As a booking approver, I want to approve a pending booking request, so that the requester can use the requested university resource.
Acceptance criteria:
- Only users with booking approver permission can approve requests.
- Only requests in Pending status can be approved.
- Before approval, the backend revalidates resource availability, capacity and applicable restrictions.
- A successful approval changes the request status to Approved.
- The approval records the responsible approver and decision timestamp.
- The approval is recorded in the request status history.
- The system prevents approval when the requested period conflicts with an existing approved reservation or active administrative block.
- The approver receives confirmation that the decision was recorded successfully.

title: Reject a booking request with a justification.
description:
As a booking approver, I want to reject a pending booking request and provide a justification, so that the requester understands why the requested resource cannot be assigned.
Acceptance criteria:
- Only users with booking approver permission can reject requests.
- Only requests in Pending status can be rejected.
- The approver must provide a rejection justification before confirming the decision.
- The system changes the request status to Rejected after confirmation.
- The rejection justification, responsible approver and decision timestamp are stored in the request history.
- The justification is visible to the requester in the request details.
- Rejected requests cannot be approved or rejected again through the same workflow.

title: Request additional information from a requester.
description:
As a booking approver, I want to request additional information about a pending booking, so that I can clarify missing or ambiguous details before making a decision.
Acceptance criteria:
- Approvers can request additional information from a request in Pending status.
- The approver must enter a message describing the required clarification.
- The request status changes to Awaiting Information.
- The message, responsible approver and timestamp are recorded in the request history.
- The clarification message is visible to the requester.
- Requests awaiting information cannot be approved or rejected until the requester responds.
- The system confirms that the clarification request was successfully registered.

title: Submit additional information for a booking request.
description:
As a requester, I want to respond to an administrative request for additional information, so that my booking request can continue through the approval process.
Acceptance criteria:
- The requester can access requests belonging to their account with Awaiting Information status.
- The response form displays the clarification message provided by the approver.
- The requester can submit a written response and update the applicable request information when requested.
- The system validates any updated dates, times, quantities and participant counts against resource rules.
- After a successful response, the request status changes to Pending.
- The response, updated information and submission timestamp are recorded in the request history.
- The request becomes available again in the administrative pending queue.
- The requester receives confirmation that the response was submitted.

title: Assign booking requests to individual approvers.
description:
As a booking office coordinator, I want to assign pending booking requests to specific approvers, so that administrative responsibilities can be distributed and tracked.
Acceptance criteria:
- Users with the appropriate administrative permission can assign a pending request to an approver.
- The assignment list contains only active users with booking approver permission.
- Each request displays its assigned approver in the administrative queue.
- Coordinators can change an existing assignment.
- Assignment changes record the responsible coordinator and timestamp.
- Approvers can filter the queue to display requests assigned to them or requests without an assigned approver.
- Assignment does not change the request's approval status or requested period.

title: Concurrent administrative decisions overwrite each other.
description:
When two approvers open the same pending request, both may attempt to make a decision using the original Pending status. The system may allow the second decision to overwrite or conflict with the first decision. The expected behavior is to accept only the first valid decision and reject subsequent attempts based on an outdated status.
Reproduction steps:
1. Two approvers open the same pending booking request.
2. Approver A approves the request.
3. Approver B rejects the request using the previously opened page.
4. Inspect the final request status and history.
Expected result: the first valid decision is preserved and the second operation is rejected because the request is no longer Pending.
Actual result: the second decision may overwrite the first or produce inconsistent history.
Acceptance criteria:
- Approval and rejection operations verify the current persisted request status.
- Only one decision can successfully transition a request out of Pending status.
- Concurrent decisions cannot overwrite an already completed decision.
- The unsuccessful approver receives a message explaining that the request was already processed.
- Automated tests cover concurrent approval and rejection attempts.

title: A booking request can be rejected without a justification.
description:
The rejection workflow may accept a submission with an empty justification when the frontend validation is bypassed or the backend receives an incomplete request. The expected behavior is to require a meaningful justification before changing the request status to Rejected.
Reproduction steps:
1. Open a pending booking request as an approver.
2. Select Reject.
3. Leave the justification field empty.
4. Submit the rejection request through the interface or directly through the API.
Expected result: the system rejects the operation and keeps the booking request in Pending status.
Actual result: the request may be changed to Rejected without an explanation.
Acceptance criteria:
- The frontend requires a non-empty rejection justification.
- The backend independently validates the justification.
- Whitespace-only values are considered invalid.
- Invalid submissions do not change the request status or create a rejection history entry.
- Validation errors are presented clearly to the approver.

title: Notify requesters when an administrative decision is made.
description:
As a requester, I want to receive an e-mail when my booking request is approved or rejected, so that I know the outcome without having to constantly check RoomBook.
Acceptance criteria:
- An approval triggers an e-mail to the requester's institutional e-mail address.
- A rejection triggers an e-mail to the requester's institutional e-mail address.
- Approval messages include the request identifier, resource, requested period and approval status.
- Rejection messages include the request identifier, resource, requested period and rejection justification.
- Notification content uses the configured RoomBook templates and sender identity.
- E-mails are triggered only after the corresponding administrative decision has been successfully persisted.
- E-mail delivery failures do not reverse the administrative decision.
- Notification delivery outcomes are available for operational troubleshooting.

title: Administrative decisions generate duplicate notification e-mails.
description:
When an approver processes a booking request, the system may send more than one notification e-mail for the same approval or rejection event. This can occur when notification processing is repeated after an uncertain provider response. The expected behavior is to send only one notification for each recorded administrative decision.
Reproduction steps:
1. Submit a booking request and wait for its administrative review.
2. Approve or reject the request.
3. Simulate a timeout after the e-mail provider accepts the notification.
4. Allow the notification service to retry delivery.
5. Inspect the requester's inbox.
Expected result: the requester receives one decision notification.
Actual result: duplicate decision e-mails may be delivered.
Acceptance criteria:
- Each administrative decision generates a unique notification event identifier.
- Repeated processing of an already accepted notification does not create another delivery.
- The notification service tracks delivery status independently of the booking status.
- Automated tests cover retries after uncertain provider responses for both approval and rejection notifications.

title: Record internal administrative notes on booking requests.
description:
As a booking approver, I want to add internal notes to a booking request, so that the administrative team can share relevant observations during its evaluation without exposing internal discussions to the requester.
Acceptance criteria:
- Approvers can add notes to requests they are authorized to review.
- Each note contains its content, author and creation timestamp.
- Notes are displayed in chronological order on the administrative request detail page.
- Internal notes are not visible to ordinary requesters through the frontend or REST API.
- Previously registered notes cannot be modified by users who did not create them, unless they have an explicit administrative permission.
- Internal notes remain available after the request has been approved, rejected or cancelled.
- Access to internal notes is restricted to authorized administrative users.

title: Optimize database queries used by the administrative request queue.
description:
Review the PostgreSQL queries used by the administrative queue and request history to identify frequently filtered and sorted columns. Add appropriate database indexes for request status, assigned approver, submission timestamp and relevant resource references. The objective is to maintain predictable query performance as the number of booking requests grows.
Acceptance criteria:
- Existing administrative queue queries are reviewed using PostgreSQL query execution plans.
- Indexes are created for frequently used filtering and sorting conditions where justified by query analysis.
- Database index creation is included in version-controlled migrations.
- Existing API filtering, sorting and pagination behavior remains unchanged.
- Database migrations can be executed in development and production environments.
- Query plans are validated after the indexes are introduced.
- Automated tests confirm that the indexes do not alter query results.

title: Configure approval routing rules by campus and resource type.
description:
As a RoomBook administrator, I want to configure which administrative approvers are responsible for different campuses and resource types, so that booking requests are directed to the correct administrative teams.
Acceptance criteria:
- Administrators can create and maintain approval routing rules.
- Each rule identifies a campus, one or more resource types and the responsible approvers.
- Rules support rooms, laboratories and equipment.
- The system applies the appropriate routing rule when a booking request is created.
- Requests are assigned to the configured approvers when a matching rule exists.
- Administrators receive a warning when a new request does not match any configured routing rule.
- Only users with system administration permission can create, edit or deactivate routing rules.
- Existing manual assignments are preserved unless an authorized user explicitly changes them.

title: Block a resource for maintenance.
description:
As a RoomBook administrator, I want to block a room, laboratory or piece of equipment for a maintenance period, so that users cannot request resources that are temporarily unavailable.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized administrators can create a maintenance block for an existing resource.
- The block requires a start date and time, end date and time, and maintenance description.
- The system validates that the end timestamp is later than the start timestamp.
- The block has an active status after successful creation.
- Active maintenance blocks prevent new conflicting booking requests from being submitted.
- The block is persisted and displayed in the resource availability calendar.
- The system records the administrator responsible for creating the block and its creation timestamp.
- Ordinary users can see that the period is unavailable without seeing restricted internal maintenance information.

title: Block university resources for institutional events.
description:
As a RoomBook administrator, I want to reserve resources for university events, so that institutional activities have priority over regular booking requests.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized administrators can create an event block for one or more resources.
- The event requires a name, description, start date and time, and end date and time.
- Administrators can associate the event with a campus and responsible organizational unit.
- The system validates that the selected resources and event period are valid.
- Active event blocks prevent conflicting new booking requests.
- Event blocks appear in the availability calendars of all associated resources.
- Event information displayed to ordinary users follows the configured visibility rules.
- The system records the administrator responsible for creating the event block.

title: View and search administrative resource blocks.
description:
As a RoomBook administrator, I want to view a centralized list of maintenance and event blocks, so that I can monitor resource restrictions and manage scheduled unavailability.
Acceptance criteria:
- The administrative interface displays maintenance and event blocks.
- Each entry displays the resource, block type, period, current status and responsible administrator.
- Administrators can filter blocks by resource type, campus, block category and status.
- Administrators can search by resource name or event name.
- The list supports sorting by start date and creation date.
- Selecting a block opens its complete administrative details.
- The list supports pagination and displays the total number of matching blocks.

title: Edit an existing administrative resource block.
description:
As a RoomBook administrator, I want to update an existing maintenance or event block, so that changes to schedules and resource restrictions are reflected accurately in RoomBook.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized administrators can edit active maintenance and event blocks.
- Editable fields include description, start timestamp, end timestamp and associated resources, subject to block type rules.
- The system validates the updated period and resource references before saving.
- Changes cannot introduce invalid resource availability or conflicting confirmed bookings without the required conflict-resolution process.
- The original block identifier is preserved after editing.
- Each modification records the responsible administrator, timestamp and changed information.
- Updated blocks are reflected in the corresponding resource availability calendars.

title: Cancel an administrative resource block.
description:
As a RoomBook administrator, I want to cancel an active maintenance or event block, so that resources can become available again when the restriction is no longer necessary.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized administrators can cancel active blocks.
- The system requests confirmation before applying the cancellation.
- The administrator must provide a cancellation reason.
- A successful cancellation changes the block status to Cancelled rather than permanently deleting its record.
- The cancellation reason, responsible administrator and timestamp are stored.
- Cancelled blocks no longer prevent new booking requests for their periods.
- The availability calendar reflects the cancellation.
- Historical block information remains available to authorized administrators.

title: Schedule recurring maintenance blocks.
description:
As a RoomBook administrator, I want to schedule recurring maintenance periods for a resource, so that regular inspections and maintenance activities are automatically reflected in resource availability.
Acceptance criteria:
- Administrators can configure recurring maintenance using daily, weekly or monthly recurrence rules.
- The recurrence configuration includes a start date and an end condition based on an end date or number of occurrences.
- Administrators can define the time interval occupied by each maintenance occurrence.
- The system generates the corresponding individual maintenance periods.
- Each generated occurrence references its recurrence configuration and original resource.
- Conflicts with existing approved bookings are identified before the recurrence schedule is activated.
- Administrators can review the generated occurrences before confirming the schedule.
- Cancelling the recurrence prevents future occurrences from being generated without deleting historical occurrences.

title: Recurring maintenance generates incorrect dates at month boundaries.
description:
When a recurring maintenance schedule is configured for a day that does not exist in a subsequent month, the system may generate invalid dates or shift occurrences unexpectedly. The expected behavior is to follow a consistent monthly recurrence rule and generate only valid calendar dates.
Reproduction steps:
1. Create a monthly maintenance schedule starting on January 31.
2. Configure the recurrence to continue through April.
3. Review the generated occurrences.
Expected result: the system applies the documented monthly recurrence rule consistently and never generates invalid dates.
Actual result: some occurrences may be assigned incorrect dates or omitted unexpectedly.
Acceptance criteria:
- Monthly recurrence handles months with different numbers of days.
- The application follows a consistent rule for occurrences falling on unavailable calendar dates.
- Generated occurrences use the configured university time zone.
- Recurrence calculations do not create duplicate occurrences.
- Automated tests cover months with 28, 29, 30 and 31 days.

title: Identify existing bookings affected by a new resource block.
description:
As a RoomBook administrator, I want to see which existing booking requests conflict with a proposed maintenance or event block, so that I can resolve scheduling conflicts before activating the restriction.
Acceptance criteria:
- When an administrator creates or edits a block, the system checks the affected resource and requested period.
- The conflict preview identifies existing approved bookings that overlap the proposed block.
- The preview displays the booking identifier, requester, resource and overlapping period.
- Pending booking requests that overlap the proposed block are also identified separately.
- The administrator can review the complete conflict list before confirming the block.
- The system does not silently cancel or modify existing booking requests.
- If unresolved conflicts exist, the administrator must follow the conflict-resolution workflow before activating the block.
- Conflict information is retrieved from current persisted booking and block data.

title: The block conflict preview omits bookings that overlap its final time interval.
description:
When an administrator creates a block that overlaps an existing approved booking only at its beginning or ending boundary, the conflict preview may fail to identify that booking. The expected behavior is to identify every booking whose occupied time interval intersects the proposed block, including partial overlaps.
Reproduction steps:
1. Create or locate an approved booking from 10:00 to 12:00.
2. Open the administrative block creation form for the same resource.
3. Configure a block from 11:30 to 13:00.
4. Inspect the conflict preview.
Expected result: the approved booking appears in the conflict list because the periods overlap.
Actual result: the booking may be omitted from the preview.
Acceptance criteria:
- Conflict detection correctly identifies partial overlaps at the beginning or end of a booking.
- Events with identical start or end boundaries follow the documented interval rules.
- Non-overlapping adjacent periods are not incorrectly classified as conflicts.
- The same overlap logic is used by block creation, editing and booking validation.
- Automated tests cover partial, complete, adjacent and identical interval boundaries.

title: Enforce resource scheduling integrity at the database level.
description:
Implement database-level safeguards and transaction handling to protect the consistency of resource scheduling. Ensure that concurrent operations cannot bypass application-level availability checks and create incompatible active blocks or approved reservations for the same resource and period.
Acceptance criteria:
- The database schema supports reliable identification of overlapping active scheduling records.
- Appropriate PostgreSQL constraints, locking strategies or transactional mechanisms are implemented based on the scheduling model.
- Concurrent booking approvals and administrative block activations cannot produce conflicting confirmed schedules.
- Existing booking and block records remain compatible with the migration.
- Constraint violations are translated into controlled API responses rather than unhandled database errors.
- Integration tests verify scheduling integrity under concurrent operations.
- The implementation is documented for future booking and availability features.

title: Resolve approved bookings affected by an administrative block.
description:
As a RoomBook administrator, I want to resolve existing approved bookings that conflict with a proposed maintenance or event block, so that the restriction can be activated without leaving affected reservations in an inconsistent state.
Acceptance criteria:
- The workflow displays the affected approved bookings identified by the conflict preview.
- The administrator can review each affected booking before deciding how to handle it.
- The system requires an explicit administrative decision for every conflicting approved booking before activation.
- When a booking must be cancelled, the administrator provides a justification.
- The affected booking changes to Cancelled by Administration status.
- The cancellation is recorded in the booking history with the responsible administrator, timestamp and justification.
- The block is activated only after all required conflicts have been resolved.
- The workflow does not automatically cancel unrelated bookings or requests.

title: Notify requesters when an approved booking is cancelled by an administrative block.
description:
As a requester, I want to receive an e-mail when my approved booking is cancelled because of a maintenance or event block, so that I can understand the change and make alternative arrangements.
Acceptance criteria:
- A booking changed to Cancelled by Administration triggers an e-mail to its requester.
- The message includes the booking identifier, resource name, originally approved period and cancellation justification.
- The e-mail identifies whether the cancellation was associated with maintenance or an institutional event.
- The notification uses the configured RoomBook sender identity and notification template.
- The e-mail is sent only after the cancellation has been successfully persisted.
- Reprocessing the same cancellation event does not generate duplicate notifications.
- Failure to send the e-mail does not reverse the booking cancellation.
- The notification delivery outcome is recorded for operational troubleshooting.

title: Confirm arrival for an approved room booking.
description:
As a requester, I want to confirm my arrival for an approved room or laboratory booking, so that the university can record whether the reserved space is actually being used.
Acceptance criteria:
- The requester can access a check-in action from an approved booking detail page.
- Check-in is available only during the configured check-in window around the booking start time.
- The system verifies that the booking belongs to the authenticated requester.
- A successful check-in records the responsible user and confirmation timestamp.
- The booking status or attendance state is updated to Checked In without removing its approval history.
- A booking cannot be checked in more than once unless an authorized administrative correction is performed.
- Users cannot check in for cancelled or rejected bookings.

title: Configure check-in windows for university resources.
description:
As a RoomBook administrator, I want to configure how early and how late users can check in for approved bookings, so that attendance confirmation follows the operating policies of each resource.
Acceptance criteria:
- Administrators can configure the permitted check-in period before and after a booking's scheduled start time.
- The configuration supports university-wide defaults and resource-specific overrides.
- The system validates that configured intervals are non-negative.
- Resource-specific configurations take precedence over university-wide defaults.
- Changes are persisted and applied to subsequent check-in validations.
- Existing attendance records are not modified when check-in settings change.
- Only authorized administrators can modify check-in configuration.

title: Check-in is rejected at the exact beginning of the permitted window.
description:
When a requester attempts to check in at the exact timestamp when the configured check-in window opens, the system may reject the operation because the time comparison excludes the boundary. The expected behavior is to allow check-in at both configured boundaries.
Reproduction steps:
1. Configure a check-in window that opens 15 minutes before the booking start time.
2. Create an approved booking starting at 10:00.
3. Attempt check-in at exactly 09:45.
4. Repeat the operation at the configured closing boundary.
Expected result: check-in is accepted at both permitted boundary timestamps.
Actual result: one or both boundary timestamps may be rejected.
Acceptance criteria:
- The check-in validation includes the exact opening and closing timestamps.
- Timestamps are evaluated using the university's configured time zone.
- Requests immediately outside the permitted interval are rejected.
- Automated tests cover both boundaries and timestamps immediately before and after them.

title: Automatically identify bookings with no confirmed attendance.
description:
As a university administrator, I want RoomBook to identify approved bookings without a recorded check-in after their permitted arrival window, so that unused reservations can be monitored and their resources can be managed appropriately.
Acceptance criteria:
- The system identifies approved bookings that have passed their configured check-in closing time without a recorded check-in.
- Eligible bookings receive a No Show attendance status.
- Cancelled bookings and bookings with a recorded check-in are excluded from this process.
- The original booking approval status and history remain preserved.
- The system records the timestamp when the No Show status was assigned.
- The identification process does not modify unrelated booking records.
- Administrators can distinguish No Show bookings from bookings cancelled by their requesters or by the administration.

title: Correct an attendance record after a no-show classification.
description:
As a booking administrator, I want to correct a booking's attendance status when a legitimate check-in was not recorded, so that attendance reports accurately represent actual resource usage.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized administrators can review bookings classified as No Show.
- The administrator can change the attendance classification to Checked In or Attendance Not Confirmed.
- A correction requires a justification.
- The system records the original classification, corrected classification, administrator and correction timestamp.
- The booking's approval status remains unchanged.
- Corrected attendance records are reflected in subsequent usage reports.
- Ordinary requesters cannot modify attendance records through the administrative correction operation.

title: Register attendance on behalf of a requester.
description:
As a university staff member, I want to register a requester's arrival manually, so that users who cannot access RoomBook at the resource location can still have their attendance recorded.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized staff members can search for an approved booking and register attendance.
- The operation records the actual attendance timestamp separately from the registration timestamp.
- The staff member must provide a justification when registering attendance outside the configured check-in window.
- The system identifies the staff member who performed the registration.
- Duplicate check-in records are prevented.
- Manual attendance registration is included in the booking history.
- Users without the required permission cannot access the manual attendance operation.

title: Record the completion of a room booking.
description:
As a university staff member, I want to record when a room or laboratory booking has ended, so that the university can maintain accurate records of actual resource occupation.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized staff members can register the end of an active checked-in booking.
- The system records the actual departure timestamp.
- The departure timestamp cannot be earlier than the recorded arrival timestamp.
- The booking attendance state changes to Completed after the departure is recorded.
- The scheduled booking period remains available alongside actual attendance timestamps.
- The system records the staff member responsible for the operation when performed manually.
- Completed bookings cannot receive another departure record without an authorized correction.

title: Record the actual number of participants in a booking.
description:
As a university staff member, I want to record how many people actually attended a room or laboratory booking, so that the university can compare planned capacity with actual resource usage.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized staff members can enter the actual participant count for a checked-in or completed booking.
- The entered value must be a non-negative integer.
- The actual participant count is stored separately from the originally requested participant count.
- The system identifies when actual attendance exceeds the configured resource capacity.
- Capacity violations are highlighted to the administrative user.
- Each registration or correction records the responsible user and timestamp.
- Reports can distinguish requested participant counts from actual attendance figures.

title: View equipment reservations awaiting pickup.
description:
As a university equipment manager, I want to view approved equipment requests awaiting pickup, so that I can prepare the requested devices and organize their handover to university users.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized equipment managers can access a dedicated pickup queue.
- The queue displays approved requests that have not yet been fully handed over.
- Each entry includes the request identifier, requester, equipment description, requested quantity, pickup date and expected return date.
- Equipment managers can filter the queue by pickup date, equipment category and request status.
- The queue identifies requests with pickup dates that have already passed.
- Selecting an entry opens its complete request details.
- Requests that have already been cancelled or fully returned are excluded from the pickup queue.

title: Notify requesters when equipment is ready for pickup.
description:
As a requester, I want to receive an e-mail when my approved equipment reservation is ready for pickup, so that I know when and where to collect the requested devices.
Acceptance criteria:
- An equipment manager can mark an approved equipment request as Ready for Pickup.
- The status change triggers an e-mail to the requester's institutional e-mail address.
- The message includes the request identifier, equipment description, approved quantity, pickup location and pickup period.
- The notification is generated only after the status change is successfully persisted.
- The system prevents duplicate notifications for the same Ready for Pickup event.
- Delivery failures do not reverse the equipment request status.
- The e-mail delivery outcome is recorded for operational troubleshooting.

title: Register the handover of reserved equipment.
description:
As a university equipment manager, I want to register the delivery of reserved equipment to a requester, so that the university can track which devices have been collected and who is responsible for them.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized equipment managers can access the handover operation for approved requests marked as Ready for Pickup.
- The operation identifies the requester and the equipment being delivered.
- The manager can register the quantity delivered for each requested equipment item.
- Delivered quantities cannot exceed approved quantities or available inventory.
- The system records each item's identification number or inventory identifier when applicable.
- The handover records the responsible manager, requester and delivery timestamp.
- The request changes to Partially Delivered or Delivered according to the quantities handed over.
- Handover details remain accessible from the equipment request history.

title: Partial equipment handover incorrectly updates available inventory.
description:
When an equipment manager delivers only part of an approved equipment quantity, the system may subtract the entire approved quantity from available inventory or fail to update the inventory correctly. The expected behavior is to adjust inventory according to the quantity actually handed over.
Reproduction steps:
1. Register an inventory containing 10 units of a particular device.
2. Approve a request for 4 units.
3. Mark the request as Ready for Pickup.
4. Register the delivery of only 2 units.
5. Inspect the available inventory and request status.
Expected result: 2 units are recorded as delivered, and inventory reflects the actual handover according to the reservation and inventory rules.
Actual result: inventory may be reduced by 4 units or remain inconsistent.
Acceptance criteria:
- Inventory updates use the actual delivered quantity.
- The remaining quantity stays associated with the approved request.
- The request status accurately reflects partial delivery.
- Repeated handover submissions cannot subtract the same quantity more than once.
- Automated tests cover partial, complete and repeated handover operations.

title: Register the return of borrowed equipment.
description:
As a university equipment manager, I want to register the return of borrowed equipment, so that the university can track returned devices and update their inventory availability.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized equipment managers can register returns for equipment that has previously been delivered.
- The return operation identifies each equipment item and its returned quantity.
- The system prevents the return quantity from exceeding the quantity currently recorded as delivered and not yet returned.
- The manager records the return timestamp and the condition of each returned item.
- The system updates the outstanding quantity associated with the request.
- A request changes to Partially Returned or Returned according to its outstanding quantity.
- Returned equipment is made available again only when its condition and administrative status permit it.
- Return records remain accessible in the request history.

title: Report damaged or missing equipment during return inspection.
description:
As a university equipment manager, I want to report equipment that is damaged or missing during the return process, so that the university can investigate the issue and prevent unavailable devices from being issued again.
Acceptance criteria:
- During equipment return, the manager can classify an item as Returned in Good Condition, Damaged or Missing.
- Damaged items require a written description of the observed problem.
- Missing items require an incident description and cannot be registered as physically returned.
- Damaged items are marked as unavailable for new equipment reservations until released by an authorized manager.
- The system records the reporting manager, timestamp, item identification and inspection result.
- The requester and equipment manager can view the recorded inspection result according to their permissions.
- Inspection information remains available in the equipment request history.

title: Damaged equipment becomes available immediately after return.
description:
When an equipment manager registers the return of a damaged device, the inventory may count it as available before the damage inspection restriction is applied. The expected behavior is to keep damaged equipment unavailable until an authorized manager explicitly releases it.
Reproduction steps:
1. Approve and deliver an equipment request.
2. Open the return operation as an equipment manager.
3. Mark the returned device as Damaged.
4. Open the equipment catalog or submit another booking request for the same device.
Expected result: the damaged device remains unavailable for new reservations.
Actual result: the device may appear as available and can be requested again.
Acceptance criteria:
- Damaged equipment is excluded from available inventory immediately after the return transaction.
- The inventory status is persisted consistently with the inspection result.
- New reservation requests cannot include damaged equipment.
- Equipment availability is restored only through an authorized release operation.
- Automated integration tests cover return registration and subsequent availability checks.

title: Send reminders for equipment returns approaching their due date.
description:
As a requester, I want to receive e-mail reminders before borrowed equipment is due for return, so that I can organize its return and avoid overdue equipment situations.
Acceptance criteria:
- The system identifies equipment requests with delivered items that have not yet been fully returned.
- Reminders are sent according to configurable notification intervals before the expected return timestamp.
- The e-mail includes the request identifier, equipment description, outstanding quantity, due date and return location.
- Fully returned or cancelled requests are excluded from future reminders.
- Each scheduled reminder is sent only once for its corresponding request and reminder interval.
- The system uses the configured institutional e-mail address and RoomBook notification template.
- Delivery outcomes are recorded and failed deliveries can be inspected by authorized administrators.

title: Implement scheduled background processing for equipment reminders.
description:
Implement a scheduled backend process in Spring Boot to identify equipment returns approaching their due dates and trigger the notification service. The process must operate independently of user requests and reliably avoid repeated processing of the same reminder event.
Acceptance criteria:
- The application includes a configurable scheduled job for identifying upcoming equipment return deadlines.
- The schedule interval is configured through environment-specific settings.
- The job retrieves only requests that meet the reminder criteria defined in HIST-066.
- Processing uses the existing external e-mail integration and notification delivery tracking.
- Repeated job executions do not generate duplicate reminder events.
- Job failures are logged with sufficient operational context.
- The process can recover from an interrupted execution without losing pending reminders.
- Automated tests verify scheduling eligibility and duplicate prevention.

title: View a university resource usage dashboard.
description:
As a university administrator, I want to view a dashboard summarizing resource utilization, so that I can understand how university rooms, laboratories and equipment are being used.
Acceptance criteria:
- The dashboard displays the total number of active resources by resource type.
- The dashboard displays booking request counts grouped by status.
- The dashboard presents approved bookings, completed bookings and no-show records.
- The dashboard displays actual recorded attendance when available.
- Equipment metrics distinguish delivered, outstanding, returned and damaged items.
- Users can select a reporting period to update the displayed metrics.
- All metrics are calculated using persisted RoomBook records.
- Only users with the reporting permission can access the dashboard.

title: Generate resource utilization reports using multiple filters.
description:
As a university administrator, I want to generate resource utilization reports with configurable filters, so that I can evaluate resource usage across campuses, buildings, resource types and time periods.
Acceptance criteria:
- Administrators can select a start date and end date for the report.
- Available filters include campus, building, resource type, individual resource and booking status.
- The report can include planned booking duration and actual recorded usage duration.
- Room and laboratory reports include booking counts, utilization duration, requested participants and actual attendance when available.
- Equipment reports include reservation counts, quantities delivered, outstanding returns and inspection outcomes.
- Multiple filters can be combined in the same report.
- The backend validates date ranges and filter values before processing.
- The report displays the applied filters and the period covered.
- Results support pagination and a total record count.
- Users without reporting permission cannot retrieve report data through the REST API.

title: Export resource utilization reports to CSV.
description:
As a university administrator, I want to export generated resource utilization reports to CSV, so that I can analyze the results in spreadsheet applications and perform additional institutional analysis.
Acceptance criteria:
- The report interface provides an option to export the current filtered results to CSV.
- The exported file includes the report period and applied filter information.
- The CSV contains the fields corresponding to the selected report type.
- Dates, timestamps and numeric values follow documented formatting conventions.
- The export includes all matching records rather than only the currently displayed page.
- Text fields are escaped correctly according to CSV formatting rules.
- The generated file uses a descriptive filename containing the report type and generation date.
- Only authorized users can generate and download report exports.

title: Export resource utilization reports to PDF.
description:
As a university administrator, I want to export resource utilization reports to PDF, so that I can share standardized reports with university departments and administrative leadership.
Acceptance criteria:
- The report interface provides a PDF export option for the currently selected report and filters.
- The PDF contains the report title, generation timestamp, reporting period and applied filters.
- The exported document includes the report results and relevant summary metrics.
- Tabular results preserve column headings and remain readable across document pages.
- The report includes page numbering and the university's configured institutional identity where available.
- PDF exports reflect the same filtered dataset shown by the report API.
- The system handles empty report results without generating an invalid document.
- Only authorized users can generate and download PDF exports.

title: Reports include records outside the selected date range.
description:
When an administrator generates a report using a date interval, records occurring near the beginning or end of the selected period may be incorrectly included or excluded because of inconsistent timestamp boundaries or time zone conversion. The expected behavior is to include exactly the records belonging to the selected reporting period according to the university's configured time zone.
Reproduction steps:
1. Open the resource utilization report.
2. Select a reporting period beginning on March 1 and ending on March 31.
3. Generate the report containing bookings and attendance records around midnight on both boundary dates.
4. Compare the returned records with their stored timestamps.
Expected result: all records within the selected local date range are included, and records outside it are excluded.
Actual result: records around the date boundaries may be missing or incorrectly included.
Acceptance criteria:
- Date filters are consistently interpreted using the configured university time zone.
- The reporting interval includes the entire selected end date.
- UTC persistence and local date conversion are handled consistently.
- The same date filtering logic is used by dashboard metrics, report tables and exports.
- Automated tests cover daylight saving transitions where applicable and timestamps around reporting boundaries.

title: View the administrative history of a resource.
description:
As a university administrator, I want to view the history of administrative actions performed on a resource, so that I can understand how its configuration, availability and usage records have changed over time.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized administrators can open the administrative history from a resource detail page.
- The history displays relevant resource creation, modification and deactivation events.
- The history includes maintenance and event block creation, modification and cancellation records.
- Booking approval decisions and administrative cancellations associated with the resource are included when the viewer has permission to access them.
- Each available history entry identifies the action, responsible user and timestamp.
- History entries are presented in chronological order and support pagination.
- Ordinary users cannot access restricted administrative history information.
- Historical entries remain available after a resource is deactivated.

title: Implement centralized and immutable audit event recording.
description:
Create a centralized audit logging mechanism in the Spring Boot backend to record security-sensitive and administrative actions across RoomBook. The mechanism must provide a consistent data structure and prevent ordinary application users from modifying or deleting historical audit records. It will support resource history, booking history and future operational investigations.
Acceptance criteria:
- The audit mechanism records the responsible user, action type, affected entity, entity identifier and timestamp.
- Relevant events include authentication, role changes, booking decisions, cancellations, resource modifications, administrative blocks and equipment handovers.
- Audit records are persisted in PostgreSQL using a version-controlled database migration.
- The application prevents ordinary users and standard business operations from modifying or deleting existing audit entries.
- Sensitive credentials, authentication tokens and unnecessary personal information are excluded from audit payloads.
- Audit recording is integrated with the relevant business transactions to prevent successful operations from silently losing their required audit events.
- Failed operations do not create audit entries falsely indicating that the requested change succeeded.
- Automated tests verify audit recording, authorization and historical record preservation.

title: Repeated processing creates duplicate audit events.
description:
When a business operation is retried after an uncertain response, the centralized audit mechanism may record the same successful action more than once. This results in duplicated entries in resource and administrative histories. The expected behavior is to maintain a consistent audit trail in which retries of the same operation do not create duplicate records.
Reproduction steps:
1. Perform an administrative action that generates an audit event, such as approving a booking request.
2. Simulate an uncertain API response after the operation has been committed.
3. Retry the same operation using the same request or operation identifier.
4. Open the corresponding resource or administrative history.
Expected result: the successful business action is represented once in the audit trail.
Actual result: multiple equivalent audit entries may appear for the same operation.
Acceptance criteria:
- Audit events support a unique identifier associated with the originating business operation.
- Repeated processing of the same operation does not create duplicate audit events.
- Different legitimate actions remain independently recorded, even when they concern the same entity.
- Existing audit records are not deleted or modified to conceal duplicate processing.
- Automated tests cover repeated requests and uncertain API responses.

title: Manage the university campus and building directory.
description:
As a RoomBook administrator, I want to register and manage university campuses and buildings, so that resources can be organized according to their physical locations.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized administrators can create, edit and deactivate campuses.
- Each campus has a name, institutional identifier and address.
- Administrators can register multiple buildings under a campus.
- Each building has a name, identifier and optional address or location description.
- A building must belong to an existing active campus.
- Buildings with registered resources cannot be permanently deleted.
- Deactivating a campus prevents new resources from being associated with it.
- Changes are persisted and reflected in resource catalog location information.
- All administrative changes are recorded in the audit history.

title: Register and maintain rooms and laboratories.
description:
As a resource manager, I want to register and maintain rooms and laboratories, so that university users can find accurate information about the spaces available for booking.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized resource managers can create, edit and deactivate room and laboratory records.
- Each resource requires a unique institutional identifier, name, resource type, campus and building.
- The registration form includes capacity, description, operating hours and available facilities.
- Administrators can configure accessibility characteristics and usage restrictions.
- A resource cannot be associated with an inactive campus or building.
- Required fields and field formats are validated by the frontend and backend.
- Newly registered resources remain unpublished until an authorized administrator activates their publication status.
- Changes to existing resources are reflected in the catalog and resource detail pages.

title: Register and manage individual equipment assets.
description:
As an equipment manager, I want to register and maintain individual university equipment assets, so that each physical device can be identified and tracked throughout its reservation lifecycle.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized equipment managers can register individual equipment assets.
- Each asset has a unique institutional identification number.
- Asset information includes equipment category, manufacturer, model, serial number and current condition when available.
- Each asset is associated with an equipment resource category from the catalog.
- The system records the asset's current inventory status, including Available, Reserved, Delivered, Under Maintenance and Deactivated.
- Duplicate institutional identification numbers are rejected.
- Equipment assets can be updated without changing their historical handover and return records.
- The asset detail page displays its current status and associated request history to authorized users.

title: Configure resource facilities and equipment specifications.
description:
As a resource manager, I want to manage structured facilities and specifications for university resources, so that users can evaluate whether a resource meets their academic and operational requirements.
Acceptance criteria:
- Resource managers can configure facilities for rooms and laboratories, such as projectors, computers, whiteboards and internet access.
- Equipment categories support configurable specifications relevant to their type.
- Administrators can associate multiple facilities and specifications with a resource.
- Users can see the configured information on resource detail pages.
- Catalog filters can use supported structured facilities and specifications.
- Removing a facility from a resource does not delete historical booking information.
- Only authorized resource managers can change these configurations.

title: Deactivate and reactivate university resources.
description:
As a resource manager, I want to deactivate or reactivate a university resource, so that resources that are temporarily or permanently unavailable can be managed without losing their historical information.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized resource managers can deactivate active resources.
- The system displays existing approved bookings and pending requests associated with the resource before deactivation.
- The administrator must review and resolve any scheduling conflicts before completing deactivation.
- Deactivated resources cannot receive new booking requests.
- Previously registered requests, attendance records and audit history remain available.
- An authorized resource manager can reactivate a deactivated resource after verifying its registration information.
- Reactivation does not automatically restore cancelled reservations.
- Every activation or deactivation is recorded in the audit history with its responsible user and timestamp.

title: Deactivated resources remain available in catalog searches.
description:
After a resource manager deactivates a resource, the resource may continue appearing in catalog search results or remain accessible through previously generated search URLs. The expected behavior is to exclude deactivated resources from ordinary user discovery while preserving access for authorized administrators.
Reproduction steps:
1. Open the resource catalog as an ordinary university user.
2. Locate an active room or equipment item.
3. Deactivate the resource as an authorized resource manager.
4. Repeat the original catalog search and access the resource detail URL directly.
Expected result: the resource no longer appears in ordinary catalog results, and ordinary users cannot access its active booking information.
Actual result: the resource may remain visible or accessible.
Acceptance criteria:
- Catalog searches exclude deactivated resources by default.
- Direct resource detail requests enforce publication and activation permissions.
- Authorized administrators can still locate deactivated resources through administrative searches.
