- Existing booking histories remain accessible to users with appropriate permissions.
- Automated tests cover catalog searches, pagination and direct resource access after deactivation.

title: Integrate object storage for resource attachments.
description:
Implement an object storage integration for files associated with university resources. Provide a backend service responsible for uploading, retrieving and deleting files while keeping storage credentials and access configuration outside source control. The integration will support resource photographs, floor plans, equipment manuals and future booking attachments.
Acceptance criteria:
- The backend supports uploading files to the configured object storage provider.
- Storage credentials are obtained from environment-specific secure configuration.
- The service generates unique storage identifiers for uploaded files.
- File metadata, including name, MIME type, size and storage identifier, can be persisted in PostgreSQL.
- File retrieval is restricted through authorized backend operations or controlled temporary access links.
- The integration handles provider errors without leaving inconsistent attachment metadata.
- The service supports file deletion according to the application's retention rules.
- Development and testing environments can use separate storage configurations.
- Integration tests cover successful upload, retrieval and failure scenarios.

title: Upload photographs and documents to resource profiles.
description:
As a resource manager, I want to attach photographs, floor plans and supporting documents to resource profiles, so that university users can understand the physical characteristics and requirements of each resource before making a booking.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized resource managers can upload multiple files to a resource profile.
- Supported file categories include photographs, floor plans, equipment manuals and usage instructions.
- The interface accepts only configured file formats and enforces the maximum file size.
- Uploaded files are stored through the object storage integration established in HIST-082.
- The resource detail page displays photographs and provides access to permitted documents.
- Resource managers can replace or remove attachments.
- Each attachment displays its filename and category.
- File access is restricted according to the resource's publication status and the user's permissions.
- Attachment changes are recorded in the resource audit history.

title: Private resource attachments can be accessed without authorization.
description:
When a user obtains the storage URL of a restricted resource attachment, the file may remain accessible without verifying the user's permissions. The expected behavior is to enforce RoomBook access permissions before allowing retrieval of protected files.
Reproduction steps:
1. Register a restricted resource attachment as an administrator.
2. Obtain the attachment URL through an authorized session.
3. Sign out and open the same URL in an unauthenticated browser session.
4. Repeat the operation using an authenticated account without the required permissions.
Expected result: unauthorized users cannot retrieve the protected attachment.
Actual result: the file may be displayed or downloaded without authorization.
Acceptance criteria:
- Protected attachments require a valid authorization check before retrieval.
- Storage objects are not publicly accessible when their category requires restricted access.
- Temporary access links expire according to the configured security policy.
- Removing an attachment prevents subsequent authorized application retrieval.
- Automated security tests cover unauthenticated access, insufficient permissions and expired access links.

title: Submit recurring booking requests.
description:
As a university user, I want to request a room or laboratory for recurring dates, so that I can organize activities that take place regularly without submitting a separate request for every occurrence.
Acceptance criteria:
- The booking form supports recurring requests in addition to individual bookings.
- Users can configure daily, weekly or monthly recurrence.
- Weekly recurrence allows selection of specific weekdays.
- Monthly recurrence allows selection of a calendar day or a weekday occurrence within the month.
- The user must provide a recurrence start date and an end date or maximum number of occurrences.
- Every occurrence is validated against resource availability, operating hours, capacity and applicable booking policies.
- The system identifies conflicting occurrences before submission.
- The requester can review all generated dates and periods before confirming submission.
- A successful submission creates a recurring booking series with individual linked booking occurrences.
- The series and its occurrences have identifiable records and an initial Pending status.

title: Manage individual occurrences of a recurring booking.
description:
As a requester, I want to modify or cancel individual occurrences of an approved recurring booking, so that changes to one activity do not unnecessarily affect the entire recurring schedule.
Acceptance criteria:
- The requester can view all occurrences associated with a recurring booking series.
- The interface allows selecting an individual occurrence for modification or cancellation.
- Individual modifications are subject to the same booking validation rules used by HIST-021.
- Cancelling an individual occurrence does not automatically cancel the remaining series occurrences.
- The system preserves the original recurrence configuration and records the occurrence-specific change.
- Administrators can identify occurrences that have been modified or cancelled individually.
- Every modification or cancellation records its responsible user, timestamp and justification when required.
- Occurrence-specific changes are reflected in the resource availability calendar.

title: Regenerating a recurring series duplicates previously modified occurrences.
description:
When a recurring booking series is edited, the system may regenerate its occurrences without considering existing occurrence-specific modifications or cancellations. This can create duplicate bookings or restore dates that were previously cancelled. The expected behavior is to preserve existing occurrence records and their individual changes when updating a series.
Reproduction steps:
1. Create and approve a recurring booking series with multiple weekly occurrences.
2. Cancel one occurrence and modify the date of another.
3. Edit the recurrence end date to include additional occurrences.
4. Review the series and resource availability calendar.
Expected result: the cancelled occurrence remains cancelled, the modified occurrence retains its updated period, and only the newly required occurrences are generated.
Actual result: duplicate occurrences may be created or previous individual changes may be overwritten.
Acceptance criteria:
- Series updates preserve existing occurrence identifiers.
- Individual cancellation and modification records remain intact.
- Only missing occurrences are generated when extending a recurrence.
- Regeneration does not create duplicate active bookings.
- Automated tests cover recurrence extension, shortening and changes to recurrence rules.

title: Configure booking policies for university resources.
description:
As a RoomBook administrator, I want to define booking policies for resources and resource categories, so that reservation rules reflect the operational requirements established by the university.
Acceptance criteria:
- Administrators can create, edit, activate and deactivate booking policies.
- Policies can define maximum booking duration, minimum advance notice and maximum advance booking period.
- Policies can define permitted booking days and time intervals.
- Policies can specify the maximum number of simultaneous active bookings per requester.
- Policies can restrict booking eligibility to selected institutional roles or groups.
- Administrators can associate policies with individual resources or resource categories.
- The system identifies the effective policy applied to a resource.
- Policy changes are recorded in the audit history.
- Existing approved reservations are not silently modified when a policy changes.

title: Apply booking policies according to requester eligibility.
description:
As a RoomBook administrator, I want booking policies to be evaluated according to the requester's institutional role and group, so that different university communities can have appropriate resource access conditions.
Acceptance criteria:
- The backend identifies the requester's effective institutional roles and groups using authenticated identity information.
- The system evaluates resource-specific policies before applicable category-level or university-wide defaults according to the documented policy precedence.
- Policies can restrict access to one or more institutional groups.
- A requester who does not satisfy eligibility requirements cannot submit the restricted booking request.
- Users with multiple roles receive only the permissions and exceptions explicitly defined by the active policies.
- The API returns an explanatory validation message when a policy prevents submission.
- Policy evaluation is performed by the backend and cannot be bypassed by modifying frontend requests.
- Automated tests cover different combinations of roles, groups and policy precedence.

title: Editing a pending booking bypasses configured reservation policies.
description:
When a requester edits an existing pending booking, the update operation may validate availability but fail to reapply the active booking policies. Consequently, users may change their requested period or details beyond the limits established by the university. The expected behavior is to validate every edited request against the current applicable policies.
Reproduction steps:
1. Configure a policy limiting booking duration to two hours.
2. Submit a valid one-hour booking request.
3. Open the pending request and edit its requested duration to three hours.
4. Submit the updated request.
Expected result: the update is rejected because the resulting duration exceeds the active policy.
Actual result: the system may accept the modification.
Acceptance criteria:
- Pending request updates evaluate all applicable active booking policies.
- The backend applies the same policy validation to request creation and modification.
- Invalid updates do not alter the persisted request.
- The requester receives an explanatory message identifying the violated policy.
- Automated tests cover duration, advance notice, advance booking limits and requester eligibility during updates.

title: Implement transactional event delivery for booking notifications.
description:
Implement a transactional outbox mechanism in the Spring Boot backend to ensure that business events requiring notifications are reliably published after database transactions are committed. The mechanism will support booking changes, administrative decisions, equipment reminders and future availability notifications without losing events when external services are temporarily unavailable.
Acceptance criteria:
- A PostgreSQL outbox table stores events generated by relevant business operations.
- The business operation and its corresponding outbox event are persisted within the same database transaction.
- A background processor retrieves pending events and forwards them to the appropriate notification handlers.
- Successfully processed events are marked with their processing status and timestamp.
- Failed events remain available for retry according to a configurable retry policy.
- Event processing uses unique identifiers to prevent duplicate notification operations.
- Failed event processing does not roll back an already committed business transaction.
- Operational logs expose processing failures and retry information without recording sensitive credentials.
- Automated integration tests verify transaction consistency, recovery and duplicate prevention.

title: Join a waitlist for an unavailable resource period.
description:
As a university user, I want to join a waitlist when a resource is unavailable for my preferred period, so that I can be informed when the requested time becomes available.
Acceptance criteria:
- Users can join a waitlist from a resource availability calendar when the selected period is unavailable because of an approved booking or administrative block.
- The waitlist entry identifies the resource, requested period and authenticated requester.
- Users must provide a valid booking purpose and participant count or equipment quantity when applicable.
- The system checks resource eligibility and booking policies when creating the waitlist entry.
- A user cannot create duplicate active waitlist entries for the same resource and period.
- Joining a waitlist does not create an approved booking or guarantee access to the resource.
- The system records the creation timestamp and initial waitlist status.
- Users can view and cancel their own active waitlist entries.

title: View waitlist position and status.
description:
As a university user, I want to view the status and position of my waitlist entries, so that I can understand my place in the queue and whether a resource may become available for my requested period.
Acceptance criteria:
- The user can access a dedicated list of their waitlist entries.
- Each entry displays its resource, requested period, creation date and current status.
- Active entries display their position in the waitlist according to the configured prioritization rules.
- The interface identifies entries that have received an availability invitation.
- Cancelled, expired and fulfilled entries are displayed with their corresponding status when historical visibility is permitted.
- Waitlist positions are recalculated when an entry is cancelled, expired or fulfilled.
- Users cannot access another person's waitlist records through the API or interface.
- Changes to waitlist position do not alter the original creation timestamp.

title: Notify waitlisted users when a resource becomes available.
description:
As a university user on a waitlist, I want to receive an e-mail when my requested resource period becomes available, so that I can submit a booking request before the opportunity is offered to other users.
Acceptance criteria:
- Availability changes caused by booking cancellations or administrative block cancellations trigger a waitlist availability check.
- The system identifies active waitlist entries matching the released resource and period.
- Eligible entries are processed according to the configured waitlist priority rules.
- The notification includes the resource, available period, booking instructions and response deadline.
- The system creates an availability invitation with a unique identifier and expiration timestamp.
- The invitation is delivered through the transactional event mechanism established in HIST-091.
- The system records invitation status and delivery outcome.
- An invitation does not automatically approve a booking.
- Expired invitations cannot be used to submit a booking request under the associated priority privilege.

title: Multiple waitlisted users receive the same priority invitation.
description:
When a resource period becomes available, concurrent availability processing may send invitations to several users with the same first-priority position. This can violate the configured waitlist order and cause multiple users to believe they have the same booking opportunity. The expected behavior is to process invitations in priority order and enforce the configured response window before advancing to the next eligible user.
Reproduction steps:
1. Create multiple waitlist entries for the same resource and period.
2. Cancel the approved booking occupying that period.
3. Trigger multiple availability-processing executions concurrently.
4. Inspect the generated invitations and their priority positions.
Expected result: the system creates invitations according to the configured priority sequence without granting multiple users the same exclusive priority opportunity.
Actual result: multiple users may receive equivalent first-priority invitations.
Acceptance criteria:
- Waitlist processing is coordinated for each resource and requested period.
- Only the highest-priority eligible entry receives the active invitation when exclusive priority is configured.
- The next invitation is issued after the previous invitation expires, is declined or is otherwise resolved.
- Concurrent processing cannot create conflicting active invitations.
- Previously processed invitation events are not duplicated.
- Automated tests cover concurrent availability events and waitlist ordering.

title: Request changes to an approved booking.
description:
As a requester, I want to propose changes to one of my approved bookings, so that I can adjust the resource period or booking details without submitting an unrelated new request.
Acceptance criteria:
- The requester can submit a modification proposal for an approved booking belonging to their account.
- Permitted modifications include requested date, start time, end time, purpose and participant count or equipment quantity when applicable.
- The requester must provide a justification for the modification.
- The proposed changes are validated against resource availability and applicable booking policies.
- Submitting a modification creates a separate pending modification record associated with the original booking.
- The original approved booking remains active and unchanged until the modification is approved.
- A booking cannot have multiple unresolved modification proposals unless explicitly permitted by an administrative configuration.
- The requester can view the proposed changes and their current modification status.

title: Review and decide on approved booking modification requests.
description:
As a booking approver, I want to review and approve or reject proposed changes to approved bookings, so that modifications follow the same administrative controls as original reservations.
Acceptance criteria:
- Approvers can access a queue of pending booking modification proposals.
- Each entry identifies the original booking, requester, currently approved details and proposed changes.
- Approvers can compare the original and proposed booking information before deciding.
- Approval revalidates current resource availability and booking policies.
- An approved modification updates the original booking details and records the decision in its history.
- A rejected modification requires a justification and preserves the original approved booking without changes.
- The decision records the responsible approver, timestamp and justification when applicable.
- Requesters receive the updated modification status through RoomBook.
- Only users with booking approver permission can decide on modification proposals.

title: Rejecting a modification proposal incorrectly cancels the original booking.
description:
When an approver rejects a proposed modification to an approved booking, the system may incorrectly apply a cancellation or status transition to the original reservation. The expected behavior is to reject only the modification proposal and preserve the original approved booking and its existing schedule.
Reproduction steps:
1. Submit and obtain approval for a booking.
2. Submit a modification proposal for its date or time.
3. Open the proposal as a booking approver.
4. Reject the proposed modification with a justification.
5. Inspect the original booking and resource availability calendar.
Expected result: the modification proposal is Rejected, while the original booking remains Approved with its original period.
Actual result: the original booking may be cancelled or have its schedule modified.
Acceptance criteria:
- Rejecting a modification changes only the modification record and its history.
- The original booking retains its previous approved status and schedule.
- The original resource availability remains occupied by the approved booking.
- Rejection does not generate a booking cancellation notification.
- Automated integration tests cover rejected modification proposals and their effects on availability.

title: View the complete history of booking modifications.
description:
As a requester, I want to view the history of modification proposals associated with my bookings, so that I can understand which changes were requested and which were accepted or rejected.
Acceptance criteria:
- The booking detail page displays all modification proposals associated with that booking.
- Each entry includes its submission timestamp, requester justification and current status.
- Approved proposals display the resulting booking information and responsible approver.
- Rejected proposals display the recorded rejection justification when visible to the requester.
- The history distinguishes original booking information from subsequently approved modifications.
- Modification history is presented in chronological order.
- Authorized administrators can inspect the complete modification history of bookings within their responsibilities.
- Historical modification records cannot be deleted through ordinary booking operations.

title: Reuse details from a previous booking.
description:
As a university user, I want to create a new booking request using the information from one of my previous bookings, so that I can repeat recurring academic or institutional activities without entering the same details again.
Acceptance criteria:
- The requester can select an eligible previous booking from their booking history.
- The system creates a new booking draft using the previous resource, purpose and relevant booking details.
- The user can change the resource, period, participant count or equipment quantity before submission.
- Original booking identifiers, approval decisions and attendance records are not copied into the new draft.
- The new request receives its own unique identifier after submission.
- All current availability, eligibility and booking policy validations are executed before the new request is accepted.
- The previous booking remains unchanged.
- The requester must review and confirm the new request before submission.

title: View a personal booking dashboard.
description:
As a university user, I want to view a dashboard containing my booking requests and reservations, so that I can manage my upcoming activities and review previous resource usage.
Acceptance criteria:
- The dashboard displays bookings belonging to the authenticated user.
- Upcoming bookings are displayed separately from past bookings.
- Each entry includes the request identifier, resource name, requested period and current status.
- Pending modification proposals are indicated alongside their associated bookings.
- Bookings with No Show, Checked In and Completed attendance states display their corresponding attendance information.
- Selecting a booking opens its complete details.
- The dashboard supports pagination when the user has multiple records.
- Users cannot retrieve another user's bookings through the dashboard API.

title: Search and filter personal booking history.
description:
As a university user, I want to search and filter my booking history by resource, status, resource type and date range, so that I can find specific reservations without navigating through every record.
Acceptance criteria:
- The booking history provides a search field for resource names and booking identifiers.
- Users can filter records by booking status and resource type.
- Users can specify a start date and end date to filter booking records.
- Multiple filters can be applied simultaneously.
- Clearing a filter does not remove other active filter conditions.
- Search and filter parameters are processed by the backend.
- Results support pagination and display the total number of matching records.
- The selected filters remain visible while navigating between result pages.

title: Personal booking history displays records outside the selected date range.
description:
When a user filters their booking history by date, reservations close to midnight may appear outside the selected period or valid records may be omitted due to inconsistent date conversion. The expected behavior is to apply the selected dates using the university's configured time zone.
Reproduction steps:
1. Open personal booking history.
2. Select a date range covering a specific calendar day.
3. Include bookings created or scheduled close to midnight.
4. Inspect the returned records.
Expected result: every record belonging to the selected local date range is displayed, and records outside that range are excluded.
Actual result: records near the date boundaries may be incorrectly included or excluded.
Acceptance criteria:
- Date filtering uses the configured university time zone.
- The selected end date includes the entire calendar day.
- Date conversion is consistent between frontend and backend.
- Pagination and total record counts reflect the corrected filtered dataset.
- Automated tests cover timestamps around both date boundaries.

title: Export personal bookings to an external calendar.
description:
As a university user, I want to export my approved bookings in the iCalendar format, so that I can add university reservations to my personal calendar application.
Acceptance criteria:
- The personal booking dashboard provides an option to export eligible bookings as an .ics file.
- Users can export an individual booking or all their eligible upcoming bookings.
- Each calendar event includes the resource name, scheduled start and end timestamps, location and booking purpose when permitted.
- Events include a stable unique identifier so that repeated imports can be recognized by compatible calendar applications.
- Cancelled, rejected and pending requests are excluded from the default export.
- Calendar timestamps include the correct time zone information.
- The file follows the iCalendar format specification.
- The export contains only bookings belonging to the authenticated user.

title: Calendar exports shift booking times during time zone conversion.
description:
When a user exports a booking to an .ics file, the event may appear at a different local time in the destination calendar because the generated file incorrectly converts stored timestamps or omits the configured time zone. The expected behavior is for imported events to retain the original scheduled local date and time.
Reproduction steps:
1. Create and approve a booking for a specific local time.
2. Export the booking through the personal calendar integration.
3. Import the generated .ics file into an external calendar application.
4. Compare the imported event with the original RoomBook schedule.
Expected result: the external calendar displays the same local start and end times as RoomBook.
Actual result: the imported event may be shifted by a time zone offset.
Acceptance criteria:
- Generated calendar events use valid iCalendar date and time representations.
- Time zone information is consistent with the university configuration.
- UTC conversions preserve the original scheduled instant.
- All-day and timed events are represented according to their respective format rules.
- Automated tests cover exports around midnight and different time zone offsets.

title: Cancel an approved booking before its scheduled period.
description:
As a requester, I want to cancel one of my approved bookings, so that I can release a resource when my academic or institutional activity is no longer necessary.
Acceptance criteria:
- The requester can access a cancellation action for an approved booking belonging to their account.
- The requester must provide a cancellation reason.
- The system verifies the cancellation deadline defined by the applicable booking policy.
- When the request satisfies the cancellation rules, the booking status changes to Cancelled.
- The responsible requester, cancellation timestamp and reason are recorded in the booking history.
- The resource availability calendar is updated after successful cancellation.
- Cancelled bookings cannot be checked in or modified as approved reservations.
- The operation does not modify other bookings associated with the same requester.

title: Configure cancellation policies for approved bookings.
description:
As a RoomBook administrator, I want to configure cancellation rules for university resources, so that requesters know the conditions under which approved bookings can be cancelled.
Acceptance criteria:
- Administrators can create and maintain cancellation policies.
- Policies can define the minimum advance notice required for requester-initiated cancellation.
- Policies can be associated with individual resources, resource categories or university-wide defaults.
- Administrators can define whether cancellation after the deadline requires administrative approval.
- The system applies the documented precedence rules when multiple policies match a booking.
- The effective cancellation policy is displayed in the booking details.
- Policy changes do not automatically cancel or modify existing approved bookings.
- All policy changes are recorded in the administrative audit history.

title: The cancellation endpoint ignores the configured cancellation deadline.
description:
When a requester submits a cancellation after the permitted deadline, the backend may cancel the approved booking without applying the active cancellation policy. The expected behavior is to enforce the same cancellation rules in the API regardless of the interface used.
Reproduction steps:
1. Configure a cancellation policy requiring administrative approval for cancellations within 24 hours of the booking.
2. Create and approve a booking scheduled to begin in 12 hours.
3. Attempt to cancel the booking using its API endpoint.
4. Inspect the resulting booking status.
Expected result: direct cancellation is rejected or redirected to the administrative cancellation workflow according to the policy.
Actual result: the booking may be cancelled immediately.
Acceptance criteria:
- The backend evaluates the effective cancellation policy before changing an approved booking.
- Frontend validation and API validation use consistent rules.
- Unauthorized direct cancellation does not modify the original booking.
- The API returns an explanatory response when administrative approval is required.
- Automated tests cover cancellation attempts before, at and after the configured deadline.

title: Submit a cancellation request requiring administrative approval.
description:
As a requester, I want to submit a cancellation proposal when my booking falls within a restricted cancellation period, so that an administrator can evaluate my reason without automatically releasing the approved resource.
Acceptance criteria:
- The requester can submit a cancellation proposal for an approved booking when its cancellation policy requires administrative approval.
- The requester must provide a cancellation justification.
- A successful submission creates a cancellation proposal with a unique identifier and Pending status.
- The original booking remains Approved until the proposal is decided.
- The proposal is associated with the original booking and authenticated requester.
- The proposal and its submission timestamp appear in the booking history.
- A booking cannot have multiple unresolved cancellation proposals unless explicitly allowed by an administrative configuration.
- The requester can view the proposal's current status.

title: Notify requesters about cancellation decisions.
description:
As a requester, I want to receive an e-mail when an administrator decides on my cancellation proposal, so that I know whether my approved booking will remain active or be cancelled.
Acceptance criteria:
- An approved cancellation proposal triggers an e-mail to the requester's institutional address.
- A rejected cancellation proposal also triggers an e-mail.
- The message includes the booking identifier, resource, originally approved period and cancellation decision.
- Rejection messages include the administrative justification.
- Approval messages explain that the original booking has been cancelled and the resource period released.
- Notifications are created only after the decision has been successfully persisted.
- The transactional event mechanism prevents duplicate notifications for the same decision.
- Delivery failures do not reverse the administrative decision.
- Notification outcomes are available for operational troubleshooting.

title: Suggest alternative booking periods when a resource is unavailable.
description:
As a university user, I want RoomBook to suggest alternative available periods when my preferred time is unavailable, so that I can find another suitable reservation without manually searching the entire calendar.
Acceptance criteria:
- When a requested period conflicts with an existing booking or administrative block, the system can suggest alternative periods for the same resource.
- Suggestions respect the resource's operating hours and applicable booking policies.
- Suggested periods have the same requested duration unless the user explicitly changes that duration.
- Users can specify a date range within which alternative periods should be searched.
- Suggestions are ordered chronologically by default.
- The interface displays the start time, end time and date of each suggested period.
- Selecting a suggestion opens the booking form with the proposed period prefilled.
- Selecting a suggestion does not automatically submit or approve a booking.

title: Alternative booking suggestions include periods outside resource operating hours.
description:
When the alternative availability service generates suggestions, it may return time slots that overlap with existing resource restrictions or fall outside configured operating hours. The expected behavior is to return only periods that satisfy every active scheduling restriction.
Reproduction steps:
1. Configure a resource with operating hours from 08:00 to 18:00.
2. Create an administrative block occupying part of the afternoon.
3. Attempt to request a conflicting period near the end of the operating day.
4. Inspect the alternative suggestions.
Expected result: every suggestion falls within operating hours and does not overlap an approved booking or active block.
Actual result: suggestions may include unavailable periods.
Acceptance criteria:
- Alternative period generation uses the same scheduling rules as booking validation.
- Suggestions exclude periods outside resource operating hours.
- Administrative blocks and approved bookings are considered.
- Suggested periods respect configured minimum advance notice and maximum booking duration.
- Automated tests cover overlapping restrictions and operating-hour boundaries.

title: Publish interactive REST API documentation.
description:
Implement and configure OpenAPI documentation for the Spring Boot REST API using a compatible documentation library. The documentation must describe RoomBook endpoints, authentication requirements, request payloads, response structures, validation errors and authorization requirements so that frontend developers and future integration teams can consume the API consistently.
Acceptance criteria:
- The REST API exposes an OpenAPI specification generated from backend endpoint definitions.
- An interactive documentation interface is available in development and testing environments.
- Endpoints include descriptions, HTTP methods, parameters and response codes.
- Request and response schemas reflect the actual API contracts.
- Authentication requirements and protected operations are documented.
- Error responses include the documented validation and authorization structures.
- Production exposure of interactive documentation can be controlled through environment configuration.
- The documentation is updated alongside API contract changes.

title: Configure personal notification preferences.
description:
As a university user, I want to manage my notification preferences, so that I can choose which RoomBook communications I receive through the available channels.
Acceptance criteria:
- Users can access their notification settings from their profile.
- The interface distinguishes notifications for booking submission, approval, rejection, cancellation, equipment handover and return reminders.
- Users can enable or disable optional notification categories.
- Essential administrative and security communications cannot be disabled through ordinary preference settings.
- Preferences are persisted and associated with the authenticated user.
- Changes are applied to subsequent notification events.
- Missing preference configurations follow the documented default notification policy.
- Users cannot modify another user's notification preferences.

title: View notifications inside RoomBook.
description:
As a university user, I want to access a notification center inside RoomBook, so that I can review important booking updates even when I do not immediately read my e-mails.
Acceptance criteria:
- The application displays a notification center accessible from the main navigation.
- Notifications include the event category, message, creation timestamp and read status.
- Booking-related notifications provide a link to the associated request or booking when the user has permission to access it.
- Notifications are ordered by creation timestamp, with the most recent displayed first.
- The interface displays the number of unread notifications.
- Users see only notifications associated with their authenticated account.
- The notification center supports pagination or incremental loading of historical entries.
- Notification records remain available according to the configured retention policy.

title: Mark notifications as read or unread.
description:
As a university user, I want to change the read status of individual notifications or mark all notifications as read, so that I can manage my notification center and identify updates that still require attention.
Acceptance criteria:
- Users can mark an unread notification as read.
- Users can mark a read notification as unread.
- The interface provides an option to mark all notifications as read.
- Read-status changes are persisted in the backend.
- The unread notification counter updates after each successful operation.
- The backend verifies notification ownership before changing its status.
- Repeated read or unread operations do not create duplicate notification records.
- Changes are reflected when the user accesses RoomBook from another authenticated session.

title: Filter and search the notification center.
description:
As a university user, I want to filter notifications by category and read status and search their content, so that I can find specific updates within my notification history.
Acceptance criteria:
- The notification center supports filtering by notification category.
- Users can filter notifications by read and unread status.
- Users can search notifications using keywords from their message or associated resource name.
- Multiple filter conditions can be combined.
- Search results are restricted to notifications belonging to the authenticated user.
- Results are sorted by creation timestamp in descending order by default.
- Pagination reflects the active filter and search conditions.
- Clearing search criteria restores the complete notification list.

title: Inspect notification delivery history as an administrator.
description:
As a RoomBook administrator, I want to inspect the delivery history of system notifications, so that I can identify communication failures and investigate whether important booking messages were processed successfully.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized administrators can access a centralized notification delivery history.
- Each entry displays the notification identifier, event category, recipient, delivery status and creation timestamp.
- Delivery statuses distinguish Pending, Processing, Delivered and Failed outcomes, as applicable to the provider integration.
- Administrators can filter records by date range, delivery status, event category and recipient address.
- Selecting a delivery record displays its processing attempts and relevant provider response information.
- Sensitive authentication information and unnecessary message contents are not exposed.
- The interface supports pagination and sorting by creation timestamp.
- Users without the appropriate administrative permission cannot access the delivery history.

title: Retry failed notification deliveries manually.
description:
As a RoomBook administrator, I want to manually retry failed notification deliveries, so that important communications can reach their intended recipients after a temporary provider or connectivity failure has been resolved.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized administrators can select a notification with Failed delivery status and request another attempt.
- The interface displays the previous failure information before the administrator confirms the operation.
- The system verifies that the notification is eligible for another delivery attempt.
- A retry uses the original notification event and recipient information.
- Each attempt records its execution timestamp and result.
- Notifications already delivered cannot be manually resent through the retry operation.
- The operation respects the idempotency mechanism established for notification processing.
- The interface displays whether the retry was accepted for processing.

title: Manual notification retries send messages already marked as delivered.
description:
When an administrator requests a retry, the system may process a notification that has already been marked as Delivered due to an intervening automatic retry or provider response. The expected behavior is to verify the latest persisted delivery status immediately before scheduling another delivery attempt.
Reproduction steps:
1. Open the administrative notification delivery history.
2. Locate a notification initially marked as Failed.
3. Trigger an automatic retry through the notification processor.
4. Allow the delivery to complete successfully.
5. Use the previously opened administrative page to manually request another retry.
Expected result: the system rejects the manual retry because the notification has already been delivered.
Actual result: an additional message may be sent to the recipient.
Acceptance criteria:
- Manual retry operations verify the current persisted notification status.
- Delivered notifications cannot be resubmitted through the retry endpoint.
- Concurrent automatic and manual retries cannot create duplicate deliveries.
- Delivery status and retry history remain consistent after the operation.
- Automated integration tests cover simultaneous retries and outdated administrative pages.

title: Configure reminders for upcoming approved bookings.
description:
As a university user, I want to receive reminders before my approved room and laboratory bookings, so that I can prepare for scheduled activities and avoid missing reservations.
Acceptance criteria:
- Users can configure reminder intervals for eligible approved bookings.
- Supported reminder intervals include 24 hours and 1 hour before the scheduled start time.
- The system generates reminders only for bookings that have not been cancelled.
- Reminders are sent to the requester's institutional e-mail address and recorded in the RoomBook notification center.
- Reminder messages include the resource name, location, scheduled period and booking identifier.
- Each reminder interval generates at most one notification per booking.
- Users can disable optional booking reminders through their notification preferences.
- Rescheduled bookings use the latest approved period when determining reminder eligibility.
- Delivery outcomes are recorded for operational troubleshooting.

title: Schedule recurring resource utilization reports.
description:
As a university administrator, I want to schedule recurring resource utilization reports, so that administrative teams can receive updated information without manually generating the same reports for every reporting period.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized administrators can create scheduled report definitions.
- A schedule includes report type, selected filters, recurrence frequency and delivery format.
- Supported recurrence frequencies include weekly, monthly and quarterly.
- Administrators can configure the report's initial execution date and, optionally, an end date.
- The system stores the report definition and its active status.
- Administrators can edit, deactivate and reactivate scheduled reports.
- Each generated report uses the filters defined in its schedule and the corresponding reporting period.
- Changes to a scheduled report do not modify reports generated previously.
- Every schedule modification is recorded in the audit history.

title: Implement scheduled report generation and processing.
description:
Implement the backend processing mechanism responsible for executing recurring report definitions, generating their corresponding files and submitting them for delivery. Reuse existing reporting services, export capabilities, notification infrastructure and transactional event handling to maintain consistency between manual and scheduled reports.
Acceptance criteria:
- A scheduled backend process identifies report definitions that are due for execution.
- The process supports weekly, monthly and quarterly recurrence configurations.
- Report execution uses the filters and reporting period associated with each schedule.
- Generated files use the existing CSV and PDF export services where applicable.
- Processing records the scheduled execution, generation result and completion timestamp.
- Failed executions are recorded and can be retried without creating duplicate report executions.
- A recurring schedule does not generate multiple reports for the same execution period.
- The process respects the university's configured time zone.
- Execution failures are logged with enough information for administrative investigation.

title: Manage recipients of scheduled reports.
description:
As a university administrator, I want to configure the institutional recipients of scheduled reports, so that usage information reaches the departments and stakeholders responsible for resource management.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized administrators can associate one or more recipients with a scheduled report.
- Recipients can be selected from eligible institutional accounts or entered as approved institutional e-mail addresses according to university policy.
- The system validates recipient addresses before saving the configuration.
- Administrators can add or remove recipients from an active schedule.
- Changes to recipients apply to future report executions.
- Previous report delivery records preserve the recipient list used at the time of delivery.
- Unauthorized users cannot modify report recipients.
- Recipient changes are recorded in the audit history.

title: View the execution and delivery history of scheduled reports.
description:
As a university administrator, I want to view the execution and delivery history of scheduled reports, so that I can verify whether reports were generated and successfully distributed to their intended recipients.
Acceptance criteria:
- Administrators can access the execution history of each scheduled report.
- Each execution displays the schedule identifier, reporting period, generation timestamp and processing status.
- Delivery information includes the recipient list and delivery result for each generated report.
- Failed executions and failed deliveries are distinguishable.
- Administrators can inspect available failure details and processing timestamps.
- The interface provides filters for execution period and processing status.
- Previously generated report files can be downloaded by authorized administrators according to access and retention policies.
- Historical execution records remain available after a schedule is deactivated.
- The history supports pagination and is restricted to users with reporting administration permission.

title: Configure operating hours for university resources.
description:
As a resource manager, I want to configure weekly operating hours for each resource, so that RoomBook offers booking periods only when the resource is expected to be available.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized resource managers can configure operating hours for each day of the week.
- Each day supports multiple operating intervals.
- Administrators can mark specific weekdays as unavailable.
- The configuration supports different operating schedules for rooms, laboratories and equipment.
- The system validates that closing times are later than opening times.
- Overlapping operating intervals are rejected or consolidated according to the defined validation rules.
- Booking requests and availability searches respect the configured operating hours.
- Operating hour changes are recorded in the resource audit history.
- Existing approved bookings are not automatically modified when operating hours change.

title: Register university holidays and exceptional closure dates.
description:
As a RoomBook administrator, I want to register university holidays and exceptional closure dates, so that resources can be made unavailable during institutional periods when normal activities are suspended.
Acceptance criteria:
- Administrators can register a closure with a name, description, start date and end date.
- Closures can apply to an entire campus or selected buildings and resources.
- The system supports multiple closure periods within the same academic year.
- Administrators can edit or deactivate previously registered closures.
- Active closures are displayed in the availability calendars of affected resources.
- Booking requests overlapping an active closure are rejected.
- Closure dates are evaluated using the university's configured time zone.
- Every creation, modification and deactivation is recorded in the administrative audit history.

title: The availability calendar displays booking slots during university closures.
description:
When an administrator registers a university holiday or exceptional closure, the availability calendar may continue displaying available time slots for affected resources. The expected behavior is to treat active closure periods as unavailable and prevent new booking requests during those dates.
Reproduction steps:
1. Open the administrative closure management interface.
2. Register an active closure for a campus covering a specific date.
3. Open the availability calendar for a room within that campus.
4. Navigate to the registered closure date.
5. Attempt to select an available period.
Expected result: the calendar displays the closure and does not offer bookable periods.
Actual result: the calendar may display available periods and allow users to initiate requests.
Acceptance criteria:
- Active closures are considered by availability calculations.
- Affected resources display the closure period correctly.
- The backend rejects booking requests overlapping active closures.
- Deactivated closures no longer prevent new booking requests.
- Automated tests cover campus-wide, building-specific and resource-specific closures.

title: Configure buffer periods between consecutive bookings.
description:
As a resource manager, I want to configure mandatory buffer periods between bookings, so that rooms and equipment have sufficient time for cleaning, preparation and inspection before their next use.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized resource managers can configure a buffer duration for individual resources.
- The configuration supports a buffer before bookings, after bookings or both.
- Buffer durations are expressed in minutes and cannot contain negative values.
- The system applies the configured buffer when calculating resource availability.
- Users cannot request periods that violate another booking's required buffer interval.
- Buffer rules apply to approved bookings and administrative scheduling validations.
- Administrators can override buffer restrictions only through an explicitly authorized administrative operation.
- Changes to buffer configuration are recorded in the resource audit history.

title: Booking validation ignores configured buffer periods.
description:
When a resource has a mandatory buffer configured between consecutive bookings, the availability validation may consider only the original booking timestamps. This allows users to request periods that begin during the required preparation or cleaning interval. The expected behavior is to include configured buffers in every availability calculation.
Reproduction steps:
1. Configure a room with a 30-minute buffer after each booking.
2. Create and approve a booking from 10:00 to 11:00.
3. Attempt to request the same room from 11:15 to 12:00.
4. Submit the request.
Expected result: the request is rejected because the mandatory buffer extends until 11:30.
Actual result: the request may be accepted because the original booking ends at 11:00.
Acceptance criteria:
- Availability calculations include the configured buffer intervals.
- Booking creation, modification and approval use the same buffer validation rules.
- Buffer validation is enforced by the backend.
- Adjacent bookings are allowed when their periods respect the configured buffers.
- Automated tests cover buffers before and after bookings and combinations of both.

title: Search for resources available during a selected period.
description:
As a university user, I want to search for resources available during a specific date and time, so that I can discover suitable rooms, laboratories or equipment without opening each resource calendar individually.
Acceptance criteria:
- The catalog provides an availability search accessible to authenticated users.
- Users can specify a date, start time and end time.
- Users can select one or more resource types.
- The search considers approved bookings, active administrative blocks, operating hours, closures and configured buffer periods.
- Results include only resources that can accommodate the requested period.
- Each result displays the resource name, location, capacity when applicable and available period.
- Selecting a result opens the resource details or booking form with the selected period prefilled.
- The search does not create a booking request automatically.
- Results support pagination and are retrieved through the REST API.

title: Compare available resources across university locations.
description:
As a university user, I want to compare available resources across campuses and buildings, so that I can choose the location that best matches my activity requirements.
Acceptance criteria:
- The availability search provides a comparison view for matching resources.
- Users can compare resource type, location, capacity, facilities and available period.
- Results can be filtered by campus, building, minimum capacity and configured facilities.
- The comparison view preserves the selected date and time criteria.
- Users can open the details of any resource directly from the comparison results.
- Resources that no longer satisfy the selected availability criteria are not presented as available.
- The interface supports navigating between paginated comparison results.
- Comparison information is retrieved from current backend availability data.

title: Save frequently used availability search criteria.
description:
As a university user, I want to save frequently used availability search criteria, so that I can repeat common resource searches without configuring the same filters every time.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authenticated users can save an availability search with a descriptive name.
- A saved search stores its resource types, campus, building, capacity requirements and relevant facilities.
- Users can view and execute their saved searches from their profile or availability search page.
- Users can edit and delete their own saved searches.
- Saved searches do not store fixed availability results or guarantee that resources remain available.
- Executing a saved search retrieves current availability information.
- The system prevents users from accessing or modifying searches belonging to other accounts.
- Saved searches remain available across authenticated sessions.

title: Implement a validated resource import processing service.
description:
Create a backend processing service for importing resource information from structured CSV files. The service must validate incoming records, identify inconsistencies and provide controlled database persistence so that university administrators can maintain the resource catalog using institutional spreadsheets.
Acceptance criteria:
- The backend provides a reusable CSV parsing and validation component.
- The service supports configurable field mappings for campus, building, room, laboratory and equipment category information.
- Required fields and supported formats are validated before persistence.
- Existing institutional identifiers are checked to prevent unintended duplicate records.
- Import processing produces a structured result containing accepted and rejected records.
- Database persistence follows the configured transaction and error-handling policy.
- The processing service exposes sufficient information for the frontend to display import results.
- Automated tests cover valid records, missing fields, invalid formats and duplicate identifiers.

title: Import multiple resources using a CSV spreadsheet.
description:
As a resource manager, I want to import multiple university resources from a CSV spreadsheet, so that I can populate or update the RoomBook catalog using existing institutional records.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized resource managers can access the resource import interface.
- The interface accepts CSV files following the documented RoomBook import structure.
- The upload screen provides a downloadable spreadsheet template with the expected columns and formatting instructions.
- The import supports rooms, laboratories and equipment categories according to their required fields.
- Uploaded records are processed by the validation service established in HIST-134.
- The system displays an import summary containing accepted and rejected record counts.
- Invalid records are not silently persisted.
- The system identifies existing resources and applies the configured update or duplicate-handling policy.
- Every import operation receives a unique identifier and is recorded in the administrative history.

title: Repeated CSV imports create duplicate resource records.
description:
When an administrator imports a spreadsheet containing resources already registered in RoomBook, the import process may create duplicate records instead of identifying the existing institutional identifiers. The expected behavior is to apply the configured duplicate-handling policy and preserve resource identification integrity.
Reproduction steps:
1. Import a CSV spreadsheet containing several resources.
2. Wait for the import to finish successfully.
3. Upload the same spreadsheet again.
4. Search the resource catalog using the imported institutional identifiers.
Expected result: existing resources are identified and handled according to the configured import policy without creating duplicate records.
Actual result: duplicate resource entries may be created.
Acceptance criteria:
- Institutional identifiers are checked against existing database records before insertion.
- Duplicate entries within the same spreadsheet are also identified.
- The import operation follows the documented insert and update policy.
- Database constraints prevent duplicate institutional identifiers even during concurrent imports.
- Automated tests cover repeated imports and duplicate identifiers within a single file.

title: Review resource import validation results before persistence.
description:
As a resource manager, I want to review the validation results of an uploaded resource spreadsheet, so that I can correct invalid information before completing the import.
Acceptance criteria:
- The import interface displays a preview of parsed records before final confirmation.
- Each record displays its validation status and associated error messages.
- Validation errors identify the affected spreadsheet row and field.
- Valid records can be reviewed separately from rejected records.
- The administrator can download a file containing rejected rows and their validation messages.
- The system does not persist imported resources before the administrator confirms the operation.
- A confirmed import uses the validation results associated with the uploaded file version.
- The import summary is available after processing completes.

title: View the history of resource catalog imports.
description:
As a resource manager, I want to view previous resource import operations, so that I can monitor catalog updates and investigate records that were rejected during processing.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized resource managers can access the import history interface.
- Each entry displays the import identifier, filename, responsible administrator, submission timestamp and processing status.
- Completed imports display accepted and rejected record counts.
- Selecting an import opens its detailed validation and processing results.
- Administrators can download the original uploaded file and the corresponding rejected-row report when available and authorized.
- The history supports filtering by date range, processing status and responsible administrator.
- Import records remain available according to the configured administrative retention policy.
- The interface supports pagination and sorting by submission date.

title: Implement secure one-time QR code tokens for booking attendance.
description:
Implement a backend mechanism for generating and validating QR code tokens associated with approved room and laboratory bookings. Tokens must be signed, time-limited and associated with a specific booking so that attendance can be confirmed securely without exposing sensitive user or reservation information.
Acceptance criteria:
- The backend generates cryptographically secure QR token payloads for eligible approved bookings.
- Tokens are associated with a single booking identifier and have a defined validity period.
- Token signatures are validated by the backend before any attendance operation is performed.
- Tokens do not expose institutional credentials or unnecessary personal information.
- Token expiration follows the resource's configured check-in window.
- Tokens can be invalidated after successful attendance confirmation.
- Token validation is protected against replay and unauthorized modification.
- Signing configuration and cryptographic secrets are managed through secure environment-specific settings.
- Automated tests cover token generation, validation, expiration and invalid signatures.

title: Confirm booking attendance by scanning a QR code.
description:
As a university staff member, I want to scan a booking's QR code to confirm the requester's arrival, so that check-in can be registered efficiently at the resource location.
Acceptance criteria:
- An approved booking displays its attendance QR code to its authenticated requester.
- The QR code can be presented through the RoomBook interface on the requester's device.
- Authorized staff members can scan the code using a compatible device with camera access.
- The system validates the QR token through the backend service established in HIST-139.
- The booking must belong to an eligible resource and be within its configured check-in window.
- A successful scan registers attendance with the booking identifier, responsible staff member and confirmation timestamp.
- Expired, invalid or previously consumed tokens are rejected with an explanatory message.
- The resulting attendance record is visible in the booking details and history.
- The existing manual check-in operation remains available when QR scanning cannot be used.

title: A consumed QR code can be reused to register attendance again.
description:
After a QR code is successfully scanned for a booking, the system may continue accepting the same token in subsequent check-in attempts. The expected behavior is to invalidate the token after the first successful attendance confirmation and prevent repeated check-in operations.
Reproduction steps:
1. Open an eligible approved booking and display its QR code.
2. Scan the code using an authorized staff account.
3. Wait for successful attendance confirmation.
4. Scan the same QR code again using the same or another authorized device.
Expected result: the second attempt is rejected because the token has already been consumed and attendance has already been registered.
Actual result: the system may accept the same token again or create duplicated attendance records.
Acceptance criteria:
- Successfully consumed QR tokens cannot be used for another attendance operation.
- Token consumption is persisted atomically with attendance registration.
- Concurrent scans cannot create multiple check-in records for the same booking.
- Failed validation does not consume an otherwise valid token.
- Automated tests cover repeated scans, concurrent requests and expired tokens.

title: Report maintenance problems affecting university resources.
description:
As a university user, I want to report a problem with a room, laboratory or equipment item, so that the responsible administrative team can investigate and arrange the necessary maintenance.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authenticated users can create a maintenance incident report from a resource detail page.
- The report requires a title, description and incident category.
- Categories include electrical problems, furniture damage, cleaning, network issues, equipment malfunction and other facility problems.
- Users can indicate the perceived urgency of the incident.
- The report is automatically associated with the selected resource and authenticated requester.
- Users can optionally associate the report with one of their previous bookings for that resource.
- Each report receives a unique identifier and an initial Open status.
- The system records the creator and submission timestamp.
- Reports are available to authorized administrative users through a dedicated management interface.

title: Attach photographs to maintenance incident reports.
description:
As a university user, I want to attach photographs to a maintenance incident report, so that the responsible team can better understand the reported problem and identify the appropriate corrective action.
Acceptance criteria:
- Users can attach one or more photographs when submitting an incident report.
- Supported image formats include the configured JPEG, PNG and WebP formats.
- Each attachment must respect the configured maximum file size.
- Attachments are stored using the object storage integration established in HIST-082.
- The incident report displays attachment previews to users with permission to access it.
- Users can view submitted photographs without exposing their storage credentials or unrestricted storage paths.
- Authorized administrators can remove inappropriate attachments while preserving the incident history.
- Failed uploads do not create broken attachment references in the incident record.

title: Assign maintenance incident reports to responsible teams.
description:
As a university maintenance coordinator, I want to assign incident reports to responsible staff members or maintenance teams, so that reported problems have a clearly identified owner and can be tracked through resolution.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized coordinators can access the incident management queue.
- Each incident displays its identifier, resource, category, urgency, creation date and current status.
- Coordinators can assign an incident to an eligible maintenance staff member or team.
- The assignment list contains only active users or teams authorized to handle maintenance incidents.
- An incident has at most one active responsible assignment unless the workflow explicitly supports multiple assignees.
- Assignment changes record the previous and new responsible parties, administrator and timestamp.
- Coordinators can reassign incidents when responsibilities change.
- Assigned incidents remain available in the corresponding team's work queue.
- All assignment operations are recorded in the audit history.

title: Track the progress of maintenance incident reports.
description:
As a university user, I want to follow the progress of my maintenance incident reports, so that I can understand whether the reported problem is being investigated or has already been resolved.
Acceptance criteria:
- Users can view incident reports submitted through their authenticated accounts.
- Each report displays its current status, assigned team when visible and most recent update timestamp.
- Supported statuses include Open, In Analysis, In Progress, Awaiting Parts, Resolved and Closed.
- Authorized maintenance staff can change incident status according to the defined workflow.
- Status transitions record the responsible user, timestamp and explanatory comment when required.
- Internal administrative comments are not exposed to ordinary requesters.
- Requesters can view comments explicitly marked as visible to them.
- Incident status changes generate notifications through the existing RoomBook notification mechanisms.
- Historical status transitions remain accessible after the incident is closed.

title: Filter and prioritize maintenance incidents.
description:
As a maintenance coordinator, I want to filter and prioritize incident reports, so that the team can focus on unresolved problems according to their urgency, location and operational impact.
Acceptance criteria:
- The incident management interface supports filtering by status, category, urgency, campus, building and assigned team.
- Coordinators can search by incident identifier, resource name or report title.
- Incidents can be sorted by creation date, urgency and latest update timestamp.
- The interface highlights incidents that have remained unresolved beyond their configured response target.
- Multiple filters can be combined in the same search.
- Results display the total number of matching incidents and support pagination.
- Changing an incident's urgency requires an explanatory comment.
- Search and filtering operations are performed by the backend and respect administrative access permissions.

title: Save frequently used resources as favorites.
description:
As a university user, I want to mark rooms, laboratories and equipment as favorites, so that I can quickly access the resources I regularly use.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authenticated users can add and remove resources from their favorites.
- The catalog and resource detail pages provide a favorite action.
- Users can access a dedicated list of their favorite resources.
- Favorite entries display the resource name, type and location.
- The system prevents duplicate favorite entries for the same user and resource.
- Users can remove a favorite directly from the favorites list.
- The application preserves favorite selections across authenticated sessions.
- Favorites do not grant booking permissions or guarantee resource availability.
- Users cannot view or modify another user's favorites.

title: Deactivated resources continue appearing in the favorites list.
description:
When a resource manager deactivates a resource, the resource may continue appearing as an active option in users' favorites lists. The expected behavior is to distinguish inactive resources from resources currently available for discovery and prevent new booking operations against deactivated resources.
Reproduction steps:
1. Sign in as a university user and add an active resource to favorites.
2. Sign in as a resource manager and deactivate that resource.
3. Return to the original user's favorites list.
4. Attempt to open the resource or initiate a booking request.
Expected result: the resource is identified as inactive or excluded according to the favorites display policy, and new booking operations are unavailable.
Actual result: the resource may continue appearing as active and expose booking actions.
Acceptance criteria:
- The favorites list retrieves the current activation status of each resource.
- Deactivated resources cannot be booked through favorite links.
- The interface identifies inactive resources or removes them according to the configured display policy.
- Historical favorite records do not cause errors in the user's profile.
- Automated tests cover resource deactivation and subsequent favorites access.

title: Implement an automated container deployment pipeline.
description:
Create a CI/CD pipeline to build, test, publish and deploy the RoomBook React frontend and Spring Boot backend using container images. The pipeline must provide consistent deployment procedures across environments and enforce quality checks before application versions reach production.
Acceptance criteria:
- The pipeline builds container images for the frontend and backend from the version-controlled source code.
- Automated frontend and backend tests run before deployment artifacts are published.
- Container images are tagged with traceable version identifiers.
- The pipeline publishes approved images to the configured container registry.
- Deployment configurations are maintained separately for development, testing and production environments.
- Environment-specific credentials are supplied through secure pipeline variables or secret management.
- Production deployment requires the configured approval process.
- Health checks are executed after deployment to verify application availability and database connectivity.
- Failed deployments are reported and provide an actionable diagnostic log.
- The deployment procedure supports rollback to a previously published application version.

title: Configure preferred campus and catalog defaults.
description:
As a university user, I want to configure my preferred campus and default resource catalog filters, so that RoomBook opens with search settings that reflect the locations and resource categories I usually access.
Acceptance criteria:
- Users can select a preferred campus from the active university campuses.
- Users can configure a default resource type for catalog searches.
- Users can optionally select a preferred building and minimum capacity.
- The system validates that the selected building belongs to the preferred campus.
- Preferred settings are stored in the authenticated user's profile.
- The resource catalog applies the saved defaults when the user opens it.
- Users can override the default filters during an individual search without changing their saved preferences.
- Users can restore the catalog to its standard default behavior by clearing their preferences.
- Preference changes are preserved across authenticated sessions.

title: Register accessibility characteristics of university resources.
description:
As a resource manager, I want to register accessibility characteristics for rooms, laboratories and university facilities, so that users with different accessibility requirements can identify suitable resources.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized resource managers can configure accessibility information for each resource.
- Supported characteristics include wheelchair-accessible entrances, elevators, accessible restrooms, reserved spaces and accessible furniture.
- Administrators can provide additional accessibility descriptions.
- Multiple accessibility characteristics can be associated with one resource.
- Accessibility information is displayed on the resource detail page.
- The information can be updated without modifying historical booking records.
- Changes are recorded in the resource audit history.
- Resources without accessibility information are clearly distinguished from resources explicitly marked as inaccessible.

title: Filter resources by accessibility requirements.
description:
As a university user, I want to filter resources by accessibility characteristics, so that I can find rooms and laboratories that accommodate my specific requirements.
Acceptance criteria:
- The resource catalog provides filters based on the accessibility characteristics registered in HIST-151.
- Users can select multiple accessibility requirements simultaneously.
- Results include only resources matching all selected requirements.
- Accessibility filters work together with campus, building, capacity and resource type filters.
- Resources without recorded accessibility information are not presented as meeting an explicitly selected requirement.
- Clearing accessibility filters restores the corresponding resources to the search results.
- The selected filters remain visible during catalog pagination.
- The backend performs accessibility filtering using the resource information stored in PostgreSQL.

title: Establish accessibility standards for the RoomBook interface.
description:
Review the React frontend and establish an accessibility baseline aligned with WCAG 2.2 Level AA. Document implementation guidelines for keyboard navigation, semantic HTML, focus management, contrast, accessible form validation and screen reader support. Configure automated accessibility checks for the frontend development workflow.
Acceptance criteria:
- The frontend is reviewed against the applicable WCAG 2.2 Level AA criteria.
- Accessibility guidelines are documented for React components and application pages.
- Automated accessibility checks are integrated into the frontend test workflow.
- The checks identify violations involving missing labels, invalid semantic structures and relevant accessibility attributes.
- Accessibility findings are documented and prioritized for remediation.
- Shared interface components follow the established accessibility guidelines.
- The development team can execute accessibility checks locally and through the CI pipeline.
- Existing application functionality remains operational after the accessibility improvements.

title: Navigate resource calendars using a keyboard.
description:
As a university user who navigates interfaces using a keyboard, I want to move through resource availability calendars without using a mouse, so that I can independently identify and select suitable booking periods.
Acceptance criteria:
- Calendar navigation supports standard keyboard interactions.
- Users can move between dates and weeks using documented keyboard shortcuts.
- Available time slots can be focused and selected using the keyboard.
- Unavailable periods cannot be selected.
- The currently focused date and time slot have a visible focus indicator.
- Keyboard navigation does not trigger unintended booking selections.
- The selected date and time remain identifiable when navigating between calendar views.
- All calendar navigation controls have accessible names and keyboard-operable actions.

title: Calendar navigation loses keyboard focus after changing weeks.
description:
When a user navigates to another week using the calendar keyboard controls, focus may return to the document body instead of remaining within the calendar. This forces keyboard users to navigate through the interface again to reach the desired time slot.
