The expected behavior is to maintain a predictable focus position after every calendar navigation operation.
Reproduction steps:
1. Open a resource availability calendar.
2. Use the keyboard to focus the next-week navigation control.
3. Activate the control using Enter or Space.
4. Attempt to continue navigating through the calendar using the keyboard.
Expected result: focus remains on the corresponding calendar navigation element or moves to the documented next logical element.
Actual result: focus may be lost and keyboard navigation becomes unpredictable.
Acceptance criteria:
- Calendar navigation preserves or intentionally restores keyboard focus.
- Focus movement follows the documented accessibility behavior.
- The focused calendar date is visually identifiable.
- Navigation works with supported keyboard-only interactions.
- Automated accessibility tests cover calendar navigation and focus restoration.

title: Provide accessible descriptions for resource information.
description:
As a university user who uses assistive technology, I want resource information to be presented with accessible descriptions and semantic labels, so that I can understand the characteristics and availability of resources using a screen reader.
Acceptance criteria:
- Resource detail pages use semantic headings and structured content regions.
- Photographs and floor plans include meaningful alternative text when they convey relevant information.
- Resource characteristics are presented with descriptive labels and values.
- Operating hours, facilities and accessibility information can be interpreted by screen readers.
- Links and buttons have accessible names describing their actions.
- Decorative images do not produce unnecessary screen reader announcements.
- Dynamic availability information exposes its current state through accessible interface attributes.
- The implementation follows the accessibility guidelines established in HIST-153.

title: Dynamic catalog updates are not announced to screen readers.
description:
When a user performs a resource search or changes catalog filters, the results update visually but screen readers may not announce that the displayed content has changed. The expected behavior is to provide accessible feedback about search completion, result counts and empty states.
Reproduction steps:
1. Open the resource catalog using a screen reader.
2. Apply a resource type or campus filter.
3. Wait for the search results to update.
4. Observe the screen reader announcements.
Expected result: the screen reader announces the updated result count or the absence of matching resources.
Actual result: the results change visually without providing an appropriate announcement.
Acceptance criteria:
- Search results expose appropriate live-region announcements.
- Loading, successful result updates and empty states are communicated to assistive technologies.
- Announcements do not unnecessarily repeat unchanged content.
- Dynamic feedback follows the accessibility guidelines established in HIST-153.
- Automated accessibility tests cover catalog filtering and result updates.

title: Request multiple resources through a coordinated booking.
description:
As a university user, I want to request a room and associated equipment through a single coordinated booking, so that I can organize an academic activity without submitting unrelated requests for each required resource.
Acceptance criteria:
- The booking form allows users to combine a room or laboratory with one or more equipment resources.
- All requested resources are associated with a common booking request identifier.
- Each resource has its own requested period and quantity when applicable.
- The user can review the complete set of requested resources before submission.
- Availability, capacity, equipment inventory and booking policies are validated independently for each resource.
- Conflicting items are identified before submission and explained to the requester.
- The system creates linked resource booking records while preserving their association with the coordinated request.
- Each linked record follows the appropriate booking approval rules.
- The requester can track the overall request and the status of its individual resource components.

title: Review coordinated booking requests and their individual resources.
description:
As a booking approver, I want to inspect all resources associated with a coordinated booking request, so that I can evaluate whether the complete set of requested resources can support the proposed activity.
Acceptance criteria:
- The administrative request detail page identifies coordinated booking requests.
- Approvers can view all associated rooms, laboratories and equipment.
- Each resource displays its requested period, quantity and current availability validation result.
- The interface displays the overall request status and the status of each resource component.
- Approvers can inspect individual resource restrictions and relevant administrative blocks.
- Approval decisions follow the configured workflow for coordinated requests.
- The interface identifies resource components that have already received an administrative decision.
- The coordinated request history preserves all decisions associated with its individual resources.

title: Coordinated booking submission creates incomplete resource associations.
description:
When a coordinated booking request contains multiple resources, the backend may persist the main request and some associated resource records before encountering a validation or database error on another item. This leaves the request in an inconsistent state. The expected behavior is to apply the configured coordinated submission policy consistently and prevent partially persisted requests.
Reproduction steps:
1. Create a coordinated request containing a room and multiple equipment items.
2. Configure one equipment item to fail availability validation or trigger a persistence error.
3. Submit the coordinated request.
4. Inspect the main request and its associated resource records.
Expected result: the system rejects the coordinated submission without leaving orphaned or partially persisted resource associations.
Actual result: some resource records may remain persisted while the complete request fails.
Acceptance criteria:
- Coordinated request persistence follows the defined transaction policy.
- Failed submissions do not leave orphaned resource booking records.
- The main request and its resource associations remain consistent.
- The user receives an explanatory message identifying the item that prevented submission.
- Automated integration tests cover validation failures and database errors during coordinated submissions.

title: Optimize PostgreSQL indexing for catalog text searches.
description:
Review the database queries used for resource discovery and implement appropriate PostgreSQL indexing strategies for text searches across resource names, descriptions, facilities and specifications. Ensure that the search implementation supports the catalog's filtering and pagination behavior as the resource dataset grows.
Acceptance criteria:
- Existing resource search queries are analyzed using PostgreSQL execution plans.
- Appropriate indexes are created for supported text search operations.
- Index selection considers the existing catalog filters and frequently queried fields.
- Database changes are implemented through version-controlled migrations.
- Indexes do not alter search results or existing resource filtering behavior.
- Search queries are validated using representative resource records.
- Index migrations can be executed in development, testing and production environments.
- Documentation describes the indexing strategy and supported search operations.

title: Search resources using keywords and descriptive information.
description:
As a university user, I want to search resources using keywords from their names, descriptions, facilities and specifications, so that I can discover suitable resources even when I do not know their exact institutional names.
Acceptance criteria:
- The catalog provides a general keyword search field.
- Search operations consider resource names, descriptions, registered facilities and supported specifications.
- Multiple relevant terms can be used in the same search.
- Search results can be combined with the existing resource type, campus, building, capacity and accessibility filters.
- The backend uses the PostgreSQL search capabilities and indexing strategy established in HIST-161.
- Results are ordered according to a documented relevance strategy when applicable.
- Search results exclude resources that are inactive or unpublished for ordinary users.
- The interface displays an appropriate message when no matching resources are found.
- Search results support pagination and display the total number of matches.

title: Catalog keyword searches fail to match words containing different accents.
description:
When users search for resource names or descriptions using words without diacritical marks, the catalog may fail to return matching records containing accented characters. For example, searching for "laboratorio" may not return a resource described as "laboratório". The expected behavior is to provide consistent keyword matching for equivalent accented and unaccented terms.
Reproduction steps:
1. Register a resource with the description "Laboratório de informática".
2. Open the catalog keyword search.
3. Search for "laboratorio" without an accent.
4. Repeat the search using "laboratório".
Expected result: both searches return the matching resource when the remaining criteria are equivalent.
Actual result: one of the searches may return no matching records.
Acceptance criteria:
- Keyword matching handles supported Portuguese diacritical variations consistently.
- Accent normalization is applied to searchable fields and submitted search terms.
- Existing filters and relevance ordering remain operational.
- Search behavior is consistent across the catalog interface and REST API.
- Automated tests cover accented and unaccented Portuguese terms.

title: Attach supporting documents to booking requests.
description:
As a university user, I want to attach supporting documents to a booking request, so that I can provide administrative documentation required to justify or authorize my intended use of university resources.
Acceptance criteria:
- The booking form allows users to attach documents before submitting a request.
- Supported attachment formats are configured by the RoomBook administration team.
- Each file must respect the configured maximum file size.
- The system supports multiple attachments per booking request.
- Attachments are uploaded using the object storage integration established in HIST-082.
- File metadata is associated with the corresponding booking request.
- The requester can review and remove attachments before submission.
- Failed uploads do not create incomplete attachment records.
- The system displays the filename and upload status for each attachment.

title: Review supporting documents during administrative evaluation.
description:
As a booking approver, I want to access supporting documents attached to a booking request, so that I can verify the documentation required to evaluate the reservation.
Acceptance criteria:
- Approvers can view attachments associated with requests they are authorized to evaluate.
- The request detail page displays each attachment's filename, format, size and upload timestamp.
- Supported document formats can be previewed within the application when technically available.
- Other supported files can be downloaded through an authorized backend operation.
- The interface identifies unavailable or corrupted attachments.
- Only authorized approvers and the requester can access the corresponding files according to their permissions.
- Attachment access is recorded when required by the administrative audit policy.
- The original uploaded files remain associated with the request throughout its lifecycle.

title: Manage supporting documents after booking submission.
description:
As a requester, I want to manage supporting documents associated with my booking request, so that I can provide additional information when required or remove documents that are no longer relevant.
Acceptance criteria:
- The requester can view attachments associated with their own booking requests.
- Pending requests allow document uploads and removal according to the configured attachment policy.
- Approved, rejected and cancelled requests retain their historical attachments.
- Additional documents submitted after a clarification request are associated with the corresponding request history event.
- The system records the responsible user, timestamp and attachment operation.
- Removed files follow the configured retention and deletion policy.
- The requester cannot modify attachments associated with another user's request.
- Administrative users retain access to historical documents according to their permissions.

title: Register external participants for an approved booking.
description:
As a requester, I want to register external participants who will attend my approved university booking, so that the university can prepare visitor access and maintain an attendance record for people who do not have institutional accounts.
Acceptance criteria:
- The requester can register external participants for an approved room or laboratory booking.
- Each participant record includes the required identification information, such as full name and contact e-mail.
- Additional identification fields can be configured according to university visitor policies.
- The system validates required fields and prevents duplicate participants within the same booking.
- The number of registered participants cannot exceed the approved participant capacity without an authorized administrative exception.
- The requester can review and update participant records before the configured registration deadline.
- External participant records are associated with the original booking identifier.
- Access to personal information is restricted to authorized users.
- Changes to the participant list are recorded in the booking history.

title: View the external participant manifest for a booking.
description:
As a university security or reception staff member, I want to view the external participant manifest for an approved booking, so that I can verify expected visitors and support their arrival at the university.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized security and reception users can access participant manifests for bookings within their assigned locations or responsibilities.
- Each manifest displays the booking identifier, resource location, scheduled period and registered participant names.
- Participant identification information is displayed according to the user's assigned permissions.
- The manifest distinguishes expected, arrived and absent participants when attendance has been recorded.
- The list displays its latest update timestamp.
- Staff can search for participants within an authorized manifest.
- The interface prevents access to manifests associated with unrelated campuses or unauthorized bookings.
- Access to participant manifests is recorded according to the audit policy.

title: Implement secure expiring invitation tokens for external participants.
description:
Create a backend mechanism for issuing and validating secure invitation tokens associated with external participants and approved bookings. Tokens must allow eligible guests to access their invitation information and perform the permitted attendance confirmation operations without requiring an institutional SSO account.
Acceptance criteria:
- Invitation tokens are generated using a cryptographically secure random mechanism.
- Each token is associated with one participant and one approved booking.
- Tokens include an expiration timestamp and a configurable validity policy.
- Token values are not generated from predictable booking or participant identifiers.
- Tokens are stored and validated securely by the backend.
- Tokens can be invalidated when a participant invitation is cancelled or the associated booking is cancelled.
- Token validation prevents unauthorized access to other participants' information.
- Token usage and invalidation events are recorded without exposing complete token values in logs.
- Automated tests cover token generation, expiration, invalidation and unauthorized access.

title: Send external participant invitations by e-mail.
description:
As a requester, I want RoomBook to send invitation e-mails to registered external participants, so that visitors receive the information and instructions needed to attend their university booking.
Acceptance criteria:
- The requester can send invitations to registered external participants associated with an approved booking.
- Invitations are generated using the secure token mechanism established in HIST-169.
- Each invitation is associated with one participant and the corresponding booking.
- The e-mail includes the resource location, event date, scheduled period and university visitor instructions.
- The invitation provides a secure link for accessing the participant's invitation information.
- The system records the invitation creation timestamp and delivery status.
- Repeated processing does not generate duplicate active invitations for the same participant and booking.
- Cancelled bookings cannot generate new invitations.
- E-mail delivery uses the external notification service and transactional event processing already implemented.

title: Expired external participant invitations remain accessible.
description:
When an external participant accesses an invitation link after its configured expiration timestamp, the application may continue displaying protected booking information or allow the participant to confirm attendance. The expected behavior is to reject expired invitation tokens and prevent access to the associated protected operations.
Reproduction steps:
1. Register an external participant for an approved booking.
2. Generate and send the participant invitation.
3. Configure or wait until the invitation token expires.
4. Open the original invitation link.
5. Attempt to access the invitation information or confirm attendance.
Expected result: the system rejects the expired token and displays an explanatory message with the appropriate next steps.
Actual result: the link may continue to grant access or permit attendance confirmation.
Acceptance criteria:
- The backend validates token expiration on every protected invitation operation.
- Expired tokens cannot be used to retrieve protected invitation information or confirm attendance.
- Expiration checks use the configured university time zone or an equivalent normalized timestamp policy.
- Previously invalidated tokens remain unusable regardless of their original expiration date.
- Automated tests cover expiration boundaries and attempts to reuse expired invitations.

title: Register university departments and academic courses.
description:
As a RoomBook administrator, I want to maintain the university's department and academic course directory, so that booking requests can be associated with the academic units responsible for the activities.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized administrators can create, edit and deactivate academic departments.
- Each department has a unique institutional identifier and name.
- Administrators can register academic courses or programs associated with a department.
- Each course has a unique institutional identifier, name and associated department.
- The system prevents duplicate institutional identifiers.
- Deactivated departments and courses cannot be selected for new booking requests.
- Existing booking records preserve their original academic associations after deactivation.
- Administrative changes are recorded in the audit history.
- The directory supports filtering and searching by department and course name or identifier.

title: Associate booking requests with academic activities.
description:
As a university professor, I want to associate my booking requests with an academic department and course, so that the university can identify which academic activities are responsible for resource usage.
Acceptance criteria:
- The booking form allows eligible users to associate a request with an academic department and course.
- The course selection is restricted to courses associated with the selected department.
- The requester can provide an academic activity name or description when applicable.
- The system validates that the selected department and course are active.
- Academic associations are stored with the booking request and displayed in its administrative details.
- The requester can update academic associations while the request is Pending, subject to the existing modification rules.
- Academic information is preserved in booking history after a request is approved, rejected or cancelled.
- Non-academic booking requests can follow the configured rules without requiring a course association.
- Only authenticated users with appropriate booking permissions can submit academic associations.

title: Configure booking quotas for academic departments.
description:
As a university administrator, I want to define booking quotas for academic departments, so that access to shared university resources can be distributed according to institutional allocation policies.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized administrators can create and maintain booking quota rules for departments.
- Quotas can be configured by resource type, campus and reporting period.
- The system supports limits based on booking count, total reserved duration or other configured allocation metrics.
- Administrators can define quota validity periods and applicable academic departments.
- Booking submission and approval operations evaluate the applicable department quota.
- The system identifies quota violations before an approval is completed.
- Administrators can configure whether exceeding a quota blocks approval or requires an explicit administrative exception.
- Quota changes are recorded in the administrative audit history.
- Existing approved bookings remain associated with the quota period in which they were approved.

title: Monitor academic department booking quota consumption.
description:
As a university administrator, I want to monitor booking quota consumption by academic department, so that I can identify allocation imbalances and make informed decisions about university resource distribution.
Acceptance criteria:
- The administrative reporting interface displays the configured quota and its current consumption for each academic department.
- Administrators can filter results by department, campus, resource type and reporting period.
- The report distinguishes allocated quota, consumed quota and remaining quota.
- Consumption calculations follow the metrics configured in HIST-174.
- Pending requests are displayed separately from approved bookings and do not consume quota unless explicitly defined by the active policy.
- The report identifies departments approaching or exceeding their configured quotas.
- Administrators can open the associated booking records from the quota report.
- Results can be exported using the CSV and PDF reporting capabilities established in HIST-070 and HIST-071.
- Only users with the appropriate reporting and administrative permissions can access quota information.

title: Configure maintenance response and resolution targets.
description:
As a university maintenance coordinator, I want to configure response and resolution targets for maintenance incidents, so that the university can establish clear service expectations for reported problems.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized administrators can configure response and resolution targets for each incident urgency level.
- Response targets define the maximum permitted time before an incident receives its first administrative review.
- Resolution targets define the expected time for completing the corrective action.
- Targets can be configured according to maintenance category and campus when required.
- The system validates that configured durations are greater than zero.
- Changes to maintenance targets are recorded in the administrative audit history.
- Existing incidents retain their original target configuration unless an authorized administrator explicitly recalculates them.
- The effective targets are visible in the administrative incident details.

title: Monitor maintenance incident deadlines.
description:
As a maintenance coordinator, I want to monitor response and resolution deadlines for open incidents, so that I can identify overdue problems and prioritize maintenance activities.
Acceptance criteria:
- The incident management interface displays the response and resolution deadlines established in HIST-176.
- Each incident displays its remaining time or overdue duration.
- Incidents approaching their deadlines receive a visual warning.
- Incidents that exceed their response or resolution targets are identified as overdue.
- The interface distinguishes response deadline violations from resolution deadline violations.
- Deadline information is updated using the latest incident status and timestamps.
- Closed and cancelled incidents are excluded from active deadline monitoring.
- Coordinators can filter incidents by approaching deadlines and overdue status.

title: Maintenance deadlines continue counting during excluded operating periods.
description:
When an incident has response and resolution targets configured according to university working hours, the system may continue counting time during weekends, holidays or other excluded periods. The expected behavior is to calculate deadlines according to the applicable maintenance calendar and configured service schedule.
Reproduction steps:
1. Configure a maintenance response target based on working hours.
2. Register an incident shortly before the end of a Friday working day.
3. Allow the weekend to pass without processing the incident.
4. Inspect the incident's remaining response time on Monday.
Expected result: excluded weekend hours do not contribute to the elapsed service time.
Actual result: the deadline may be marked as overdue despite the incident remaining within its permitted working hours.
Acceptance criteria:
- Deadline calculations respect the configured maintenance working calendar.
- Registered holidays and excluded periods are considered when calculating service targets.
- Response and resolution calculations use consistent time zone rules.
- Incidents with paused or suspended statuses follow the documented deadline policy.
- Automated tests cover weekends, holidays and working-hour boundaries.

title: Configure escalation rules for overdue maintenance incidents.
description:
As a maintenance administrator, I want to configure escalation rules for incidents approaching or exceeding their deadlines, so that responsible teams and coordinators are informed when maintenance requires additional attention.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized administrators can configure escalation rules based on incident urgency and deadline status.
- Rules can define the responsible maintenance team, escalation recipient and notification condition.
- Administrators can configure multiple escalation levels for the same incident.
- Escalation conditions can be triggered before or after response and resolution deadlines.
- The system records each escalation event with its triggering condition and timestamp.
- An incident cannot repeatedly trigger the same escalation level for the same deadline event.
- Changes to escalation rules are recorded in the audit history.
- Only users with maintenance administration permission can modify escalation configurations.

title: Create maintenance work orders from incident reports.
description:
As a maintenance coordinator, I want to create work orders from reported maintenance incidents, so that identified problems can be converted into controlled technical activities assigned to the maintenance team.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized coordinators can create a work order from an existing maintenance incident.
- Each work order receives a unique identifier.
- The work order inherits the associated resource, incident description, category and urgency.
- Coordinators can provide a technical diagnosis, planned activities and expected completion date.
- A work order can reference one or more related incident reports when explicitly permitted.
- The original incident remains linked to the generated work order.
- Creating a work order does not automatically close the original incident.
- The system records the responsible coordinator and creation timestamp.
- Work orders are available through a dedicated administrative management interface.

title: Assign maintenance work orders to technicians.
description:
As a maintenance coordinator, I want to assign work orders to qualified maintenance technicians, so that each corrective activity has a clearly identified responsible person.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized coordinators can assign work orders to eligible maintenance technicians.
- The technician directory displays active users authorized to perform maintenance activities.
- Each assignment records the responsible technician, assigning coordinator and assignment timestamp.
- Coordinators can reassign work orders when responsibilities change.
- Technicians can access work orders assigned to them through their dedicated work queue.
- The work order displays its current assignment and assignment history.
- Assignment changes do not modify the original incident report.
- All assignments and reassignments are recorded in the audit history.

title: Repeated work order creation generates duplicate maintenance activities.
description:
When a coordinator submits a work order creation operation more than once after an uncertain API response, RoomBook may generate multiple work orders for the same incident. The expected behavior is to prevent duplicate active work orders when the same creation operation is repeated.
Reproduction steps:
1. Open an existing maintenance incident.
2. Create a work order from the incident.
3. Simulate an API response timeout after the work order has been persisted.
4. Repeat the creation operation from the incident details page.
5. Inspect the generated work orders.
Expected result: only one work order is created for the original creation operation.
Actual result: multiple work orders may be associated with the same incident.
Acceptance criteria:
- Work order creation supports an idempotency mechanism.
- Repeated submissions of the same creation operation do not create duplicate records.
- The backend validates existing work order associations before processing a new operation.
- Legitimate additional work orders can still be created when explicitly permitted.
- Automated tests cover repeated submissions and uncertain API responses.

title: Implement automated maintenance deadline monitoring.
description:
Implement a scheduled background process responsible for evaluating open maintenance incidents against their configured response and resolution targets. The process must identify approaching deadlines, overdue incidents and applicable escalation conditions, using the maintenance calendar and notification infrastructure already established.
Acceptance criteria:
- A configurable Spring Boot scheduled process evaluates open maintenance incidents.
- The process uses the deadline configuration established in HIST-176.
- Working calendars, holidays and excluded periods are respected.
- Applicable escalation rules from HIST-179 are evaluated during processing.
- Notifications are generated through the existing transactional event mechanism.
- The process records its execution timestamp and processing outcome.
- Repeated executions do not generate duplicate escalation events.
- Failed processing can be retried without losing pending escalation events.
- Operational logs identify processing failures without exposing sensitive information.
- Automated tests cover deadline evaluation, escalation conditions and repeated executions.

title: Update maintenance work order progress.
description:
As a maintenance technician, I want to update the progress of my assigned work orders, so that coordinators can monitor maintenance activities and understand which tasks are awaiting execution or completion.
Acceptance criteria:
- Technicians can access work orders assigned to their accounts.
- Supported work order statuses include Assigned, In Progress, On Hold, Awaiting Parts and Completed.
- Each status transition follows the defined work order workflow.
- Technicians can provide progress comments when updating a work order.
- Changes record the responsible technician, previous status, new status and timestamp.
- On Hold and Awaiting Parts statuses require an explanatory comment.
- Coordinators can view the current status and complete progress history.
- Unauthorized users cannot modify work orders assigned to other technicians unless explicitly permitted.

title: Record labor and material consumption for maintenance work orders.
description:
As a maintenance technician, I want to record the labor time and materials used during a work order, so that the university can track maintenance costs and understand the resources required to repair its facilities and equipment.
Acceptance criteria:
- Technicians can register labor entries associated with a work order.
- Each labor entry includes the technician, activity description, date and recorded duration.
- Technicians can register materials and replacement components used during maintenance.
- Material entries include description, quantity and unit of measurement.
- The system supports associating material costs when unit prices are available.
- Labor and material records are displayed separately in the work order details.
- Entries can be corrected by authorized users with the corresponding justification.
- Each registration and correction records its author and timestamp.
- Historical consumption records remain available after the work order is completed.

title: Attach technical evidence to maintenance work orders.
description:
As a maintenance technician, I want to attach photographs, inspection documents and technical reports to a work order, so that coordinators can verify the work performed and maintain evidence of maintenance activities.
Acceptance criteria:
- Technicians can upload multiple attachments to an assigned work order.
- Supported attachment formats include configured image, PDF and document formats.
- File uploads respect the configured maximum size.
- Attachments are stored through the object storage integration established in HIST-082.
- Each attachment includes its filename, category, uploader and upload timestamp.
- Authorized coordinators can preview or download supporting documents.
- Attachments remain associated with the work order after completion.
- File access follows RoomBook authorization rules.
- Upload and removal operations are recorded in the work order history.

title: Maintenance work order cost calculations omit registered material expenses.
description:
When labor and material consumption are registered for a maintenance work order, the displayed total cost may include labor expenses but exclude material costs or fail to update after new entries are recorded. The expected behavior is to calculate the total using all valid cost entries associated with the work order.
Reproduction steps:
1. Open an assigned maintenance work order.
2. Register labor with an associated cost.
3. Register replacement materials with unit prices and quantities.
4. Inspect the work order cost summary.
5. Add another material entry and review the total again.
Expected result: the total reflects all registered labor and material expenses.
Actual result: the displayed total may omit material expenses or show an outdated value.
Acceptance criteria:
- Work order totals include all valid labor and material cost entries.
- Material totals account for unit price and recorded quantity.
- Corrections to existing entries update the calculated total.
- Entries without an associated monetary value are not assigned invented costs.
- Automated tests cover labor-only, material-only and combined maintenance expenses.

title: Create preventive maintenance plans for university resources.
description:
As a maintenance coordinator, I want to create preventive maintenance plans for rooms, laboratories and equipment, so that scheduled inspections and maintenance activities can be organized before failures occur.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized coordinators can create preventive maintenance plans for active resources.
- Each plan includes a name, description, responsible team and maintenance category.
- Plans support configurable recurrence frequencies, including weekly, monthly, quarterly and annually.
- Coordinators can define an activation date and an end condition.
- Each plan specifies the maintenance activities to be performed.
- The plan can be associated with one or more eligible resources.
- Administrators can activate, suspend, edit and deactivate plans.
- Plan changes are recorded in the administrative audit history.
- Existing completed maintenance records remain available after a plan is deactivated.

title: Configure preventive maintenance inspection checklists.
description:
As a maintenance coordinator, I want to configure inspection checklists for preventive maintenance activities, so that technicians follow consistent procedures when inspecting university resources.
Acceptance criteria:
- Coordinators can create reusable inspection checklist templates.
- Each checklist contains ordered inspection items with descriptions and response requirements.
- Supported response types include Pass/Fail, Yes/No, numeric values and written observations.
- Checklist items can be marked as mandatory or optional.
- Templates can be associated with maintenance categories and preventive maintenance plans.
- Coordinators can edit active templates without modifying previously completed inspection records.
- The interface displays checklist instructions to assigned technicians.
- Only authorized maintenance coordinators can create or modify checklist templates.

title: Implement recurring preventive maintenance scheduling.
description:
Implement a backend scheduling service responsible for generating preventive maintenance activities from active plans. The service must calculate future occurrences, associate the appropriate inspection checklist and create records for technicians to execute.
Acceptance criteria:
- A scheduled Spring Boot process evaluates active preventive maintenance plans.
- The processor supports the recurrence frequencies configured in HIST-188.
- Generated activities are associated with the correct resources and responsible maintenance teams.
- Applicable inspection checklist templates from HIST-189 are associated with each generated activity.
- Occurrences are generated according to the plan's activation date and end condition.
- Repeated processing does not create duplicate activities for the same plan occurrence.
- Suspended and deactivated plans do not generate future activities.
- The process records its execution status and generated activity identifiers.
- Processing failures are logged and can be investigated by authorized administrators.
- Automated tests cover recurrence calculations, plan status and duplicate prevention.

title: Preventive maintenance schedules generate activities for inactive resources.
description:
When a resource is deactivated after being associated with an active preventive maintenance plan, the scheduling process may continue generating activities for that resource. The expected behavior is to prevent new maintenance activities from being generated for resources that are no longer active, while preserving their historical records.
Reproduction steps:
1. Create an active preventive maintenance plan for an equipment item.
2. Configure recurring inspections through the scheduler.
3. Deactivate the equipment item in the resource catalog.
4. Execute the preventive maintenance scheduler.
5. Inspect the generated activities.
Expected result: no new preventive maintenance activities are generated for the deactivated resource.
Actual result: activities may continue being created despite the resource's inactive status.
Acceptance criteria:
- The scheduling process validates the current resource status before generating each occurrence.
- Deactivated resources are excluded from new preventive maintenance activities.
- Historical plans and previously generated activities remain accessible.
- Administrators receive information about skipped occurrences when relevant.
- Automated tests cover resource deactivation before scheduled execution.

title: Create resource availability blocks from approved maintenance work orders.
description:
As a maintenance coordinator, I want to create an administrative availability block directly from an approved maintenance work order, so that users cannot reserve a resource while corrective or preventive maintenance is being performed.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized coordinators can create an availability block from an eligible maintenance work order.
- The block inherits the associated resource and maintenance reference.
- The coordinator provides the planned maintenance start and end timestamps.
- The block is validated against existing approved bookings and active administrative restrictions.
- Conflicting reservations are displayed through the conflict-resolution workflow established in HIST-046 and HIST-049.
- Once activated, the block prevents conflicting booking requests.
- The block references the originating work order for administrative traceability.
- The system records the responsible coordinator and creation timestamp.
- The resource calendar displays the maintenance period.

title: Complete maintenance work orders and release restricted resources.
description:
As a maintenance coordinator, I want to complete a maintenance work order and release its associated resource block, so that a repaired or inspected resource can return to normal university operations.
Acceptance criteria:
- Technicians can submit a work order for completion when all required activities have been recorded.
- Mandatory inspection checklist items must be completed before completion can be requested.
- Technicians must provide a completion summary.
- Coordinators can review completion information and supporting evidence before confirming completion.
- Work orders requiring administrative verification cannot be completed without that verification.
- Associated maintenance blocks remain active until the required completion conditions are satisfied.
- Successful completion records the responsible users, completion timestamp and final work order status.
- The resource becomes eligible for new bookings after its associated restrictions are properly released.
- Completion and resource release operations are recorded in the audit history.

title: Resource availability is restored before maintenance completion is approved.
description:
When a technician submits a maintenance work order for completion, the associated resource block may be cancelled before a coordinator performs the required administrative verification. This can make an unfinished or unverified resource available for new bookings. The expected behavior is to retain the block until all completion conditions have been satisfied.
Reproduction steps:
1. Create a maintenance work order associated with an active resource block.
2. Assign the work order to a technician.
3. Complete the required technical activities but leave the administrative verification pending.
4. Submit the work order for completion.
5. Inspect the resource availability calendar.
Expected result: the maintenance block remains active until the coordinator approves completion.
Actual result: the block may be released immediately after the technician submits the completion request.
Acceptance criteria:
- Work order submission and work order approval are distinct operations.
- Resource blocks remain active while mandatory completion checks are pending.
- Only authorized completion operations can release associated blocks.
- The resource calendar reflects the persisted block status.
- Automated integration tests cover pending verification and approved completion scenarios.

title: Generate maintenance performance reports.
description:
As a university administrator, I want to generate maintenance performance reports, so that I can evaluate incident response, work order completion and resource maintenance activity across the university.
Acceptance criteria:
- Administrators can generate reports for a configurable date range.
- Reports support filters for campus, building, resource type, maintenance category, urgency and responsible team.
- Results include the number of incidents received, resolved and still open.
- Reports display average response time and average resolution time.
- The report identifies incidents that exceeded their configured service targets.
- Work order metrics include completion counts, average completion duration and status distribution.
- Maintenance cost summaries distinguish recorded labor and material expenses.
- Preventive maintenance metrics distinguish scheduled activities, completed inspections and overdue activities.
- Applied filters and reporting periods are displayed with the results.
- Reports support pagination and export through the existing CSV and PDF capabilities.

title: Optimize maintenance reporting queries.
description:
Review and optimize PostgreSQL queries used by maintenance performance reports and administrative incident dashboards. Introduce appropriate indexing, query restructuring and aggregation strategies to support reporting across incidents, work orders, inspection activities and cost records.
Acceptance criteria:
- Existing maintenance report queries are reviewed using PostgreSQL execution plans.
- Frequently filtered fields and relevant relationships are evaluated for indexing.
- Aggregations avoid unnecessary repeated retrieval of incident and work order records.
- Appropriate indexes and database changes are introduced through version-controlled migrations.
- Report calculations remain consistent with the underlying persisted records.
- Optimizations do not change existing filters, authorization rules or export results.
- Query behavior is validated using representative datasets.
- Automated tests verify report totals and aggregation accuracy after the changes.

title: Register warranty information for university equipment.
description:
As an equipment manager, I want to register warranty information for individual equipment assets, so that the university can monitor coverage periods and identify devices eligible for manufacturer or supplier support.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized equipment managers can register warranty information for an equipment asset.
- Warranty information includes provider, coverage start date, expiration date and relevant contractual reference.
- Administrators can associate warranty documents through the existing object storage integration.
- The system validates that the expiration date is not earlier than the coverage start date.
- Equipment details display the current warranty status and expiration date.
- Warranty records can be updated by authorized users.
- Previous warranty information is preserved in the asset history when replaced or corrected.
- Warranty changes are recorded in the administrative audit history.
- Equipment without registered warranty information is clearly identified.

title: Notify equipment managers about expiring warranties.
description:
As an equipment manager, I want to receive notifications before equipment warranties expire, so that I can coordinate inspections, maintenance claims or replacement decisions while manufacturer coverage is still valid.
Acceptance criteria:
- The system identifies equipment warranties approaching their expiration dates.
- Administrators can configure notification intervals before expiration.
- Notifications are sent to the responsible equipment managers through their institutional e-mail addresses.
- The message identifies the equipment asset, institutional identifier, warranty provider and expiration date.
- Warranty notifications are also available through the RoomBook notification center.
- Each configured reminder interval generates at most one notification per warranty record.
- Deactivated equipment without an active operational management requirement follows the configured notification policy.
- Warranty changes are considered when evaluating future reminders.
- Delivery outcomes are recorded for operational troubleshooting.

title: Register equipment disposal and retirement.
description:
As an equipment manager, I want to register the disposal or permanent retirement of university equipment, so that the institutional inventory accurately reflects assets that are no longer owned or available for university use.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized equipment managers can initiate an equipment disposal or retirement record.
- The operation requires a disposal reason, effective date and responsible administrator.
- Supported reasons include permanent damage, obsolescence, loss, transfer and sale.
- Equipment with outstanding deliveries, active reservations or unresolved maintenance records must be reviewed before disposal.
- The system prevents disposed assets from being included in available inventory.
- The equipment asset receives a Disposed or Retired status according to the selected operation.
- Historical reservation, maintenance, warranty and handover records remain accessible.
- The system supports attaching disposal documentation through the existing object storage integration.
- Disposal operations are recorded in the administrative audit history.

title: Disposed equipment remains included in available inventory totals.
description:
After an equipment manager registers the disposal of an asset, the equipment inventory summary may continue including that asset in available quantities. The expected behavior is to exclude disposed and retired equipment from all current availability and inventory calculations while preserving its historical records.
Reproduction steps:
1. Register an equipment category containing multiple available assets.
2. Open the equipment inventory summary and record the available quantity.
3. Dispose of one asset through the equipment management interface.
4. Return to the inventory summary and resource catalog.
5. Inspect the displayed available quantity and asset status.
Expected result: the disposed asset is excluded from current available inventory and cannot be reserved.
Actual result: the asset may remain included in availability totals or appear as bookable equipment.
Acceptance criteria:
- Disposed and retired assets are excluded from available inventory calculations.
- Equipment reservation validation rejects disposed assets.
- Historical equipment records remain accessible to authorized administrators.
- Inventory totals are consistent across catalog searches, equipment management pages and reports.
- Automated tests cover disposal, retirement and subsequent inventory calculations.

title: Implement automated PostgreSQL backup and restoration procedures.
description:
Implement automated database backup and restoration procedures for the RoomBook PostgreSQL database. Configure backup scheduling, retention, secure storage and restoration validation to protect institutional booking and resource records against data loss.
Acceptance criteria:
- Automated backups are generated according to a configurable schedule.
- Backups are stored in an approved storage location with restricted access.
- Backup files are encrypted according to the university security requirements.
- The backup process records execution timestamp, completion status and backup identifier.
- Failed backup executions generate operational alerts.
- Retention rules define how long backup files are preserved.
- Restoration procedures are documented and tested in a non-production environment.
- Database consistency is verified after a restoration test.
- Backup credentials and encryption keys are managed through secure configuration.
- Backup and restoration operations are logged without exposing sensitive credentials.

title: Implement centralized application monitoring and observability.
description:
Configure centralized monitoring for the React frontend, Spring Boot API, PostgreSQL database and background processing services. Establish consistent application logs, operational metrics and distributed request tracing to support troubleshooting and production incident investigation.
Acceptance criteria:
- Backend application logs are centralized in the configured monitoring platform.
- Logs include timestamp, severity, application component and correlation identifier.
- Sensitive information, authentication tokens and personal data are excluded from logs.
- Metrics cover API availability, response times, error rates, database connectivity and background job execution.
- Request tracing allows related operations across application components to be correlated.
- Monitoring configuration supports development, testing and production environments.
- Operational alerts can be configured for application failures and relevant service thresholds.
- Monitoring components do not expose internal infrastructure information to ordinary users.
- Integration with the existing container deployment pipeline is documented.

title: View the operational status of RoomBook services.
description:
As a RoomBook administrator, I want to view the operational status of the application's services, so that I can identify service interruptions and investigate problems affecting university users.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized administrators can access an operational status dashboard.
- The dashboard displays the status of the frontend, backend API, PostgreSQL connection, external e-mail integration and background processing services.
- Available statuses distinguish operational, degraded and unavailable services.
- The dashboard displays the latest health-check timestamp for each monitored component.
- Service information is retrieved using the monitoring infrastructure established in HIST-202.
- The interface identifies components that have stopped reporting health information.
- Internal credentials, connection strings and sensitive infrastructure details are never displayed.
- Only users with system administration permission can access the operational dashboard.

title: Inspect database backup execution history.
description:
As a RoomBook administrator, I want to inspect database backup records, so that I can verify whether backups are being generated successfully and identify failures requiring investigation.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized administrators can access a backup history page.
- Each backup entry displays its identifier, execution timestamp, status and stored backup reference.
- The interface distinguishes successful, failed and currently processing backup operations.
- Administrators can filter records by execution date and status.
- Failed operations display available diagnostic information without exposing sensitive infrastructure data.
- The latest successful backup is clearly identifiable.
- Backup history is retrieved from the operational records established in HIST-201.
- Only authorized system administrators can access backup information.
- Historical records remain available according to the configured retention policy.

title: Publish institutional announcements through RoomBook.
description:
As a university administrator, I want to publish institutional announcements through RoomBook, so that I can communicate important operational information, policy changes and university events to the relevant user communities.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized administrators can create, edit, publish and deactivate announcements.
- Each announcement requires a title, message body and publication period.
- Announcements can target all users or selected institutional roles, campuses and departments.
- Administrators can schedule a future publication timestamp.
- The system supports draft, scheduled, published and expired announcement statuses.
- Administrators can optionally mark an announcement as requiring user acknowledgement.
- Published announcements are displayed only to their intended audiences.
- Changes to published announcements are recorded in the audit history.
- Administrators can preview announcements before publication.

title: View announcements relevant to an authenticated user.
description:
As a university user, I want to view institutional announcements relevant to my account, so that I can stay informed about university operations, resource restrictions and administrative communications.
Acceptance criteria:
- The application provides an announcements section accessible through the main navigation.
- Users see published announcements matching their institutional roles, campus and department according to the targeting configuration.
- Each announcement displays its title, content, publication timestamp and expiration date when applicable.
- Announcements requiring acknowledgement are visually distinguished from informational announcements.
- Users can open the complete announcement details.
- Expired and unpublished announcements are not presented as currently active communications.
- Users without access to a targeted announcement cannot retrieve it through the REST API.
- The interface supports pagination and sorting by publication timestamp.

title: Expired institutional announcements remain visible as active communications.
description:
When an institutional announcement reaches its configured expiration timestamp, it may continue appearing in the active announcements section because the expiration condition is not correctly evaluated. The expected behavior is to stop displaying expired announcements as active while preserving their historical records according to the retention policy.
Reproduction steps:
1. Create an announcement with a publication period ending at a specific timestamp.
2. Publish the announcement and access the announcements section as an eligible user.
3. Allow the configured expiration timestamp to pass.
4. Refresh the announcements section and attempt to access the original announcement URL.
Expected result: the announcement is no longer presented as active and cannot be retrieved through the active announcements endpoint.
Actual result: the announcement may remain visible as an active communication.
Acceptance criteria:
- Announcement expiration is evaluated using the configured university time zone.
- Expired announcements are excluded from active announcement queries.
- Direct API requests enforce publication and expiration conditions.
- Historical announcement records remain available to authorized administrators.
- Automated tests cover publication and expiration timestamp boundaries.

title: Configure academic periods for university scheduling.
description:
As a RoomBook administrator, I want to configure academic periods such as semesters and examination periods, so that bookings and institutional reports can be organized according to the university's academic calendar.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized administrators can create and maintain academic periods.
- Each period requires a name, institutional identifier, start date and end date.
- The system supports academic periods such as semesters, recesses and examination periods.
- Administrators can associate periods with one or more campuses when applicable.
- Period date ranges are validated to prevent invalid or unintended overlaps according to institutional rules.
- Administrators can activate, deactivate and edit academic periods.
- Existing bookings retain their original academic period association when periods are modified.
- Academic period information is available to booking and reporting operations.
- All changes are recorded in the administrative audit history.

title: Associate booking requests with academic periods automatically.
description:
As a university user, I want RoomBook to identify the academic period associated with my requested booking date, so that reservations can be categorized consistently without requiring me to select the academic calendar information manually.
Acceptance criteria:
- The backend identifies the academic period covering the requested booking date using the configuration established in HIST-208.
- The academic period is associated with eligible booking requests upon successful submission.
- The booking detail page displays the associated academic period.
- The association is preserved throughout the booking lifecycle.
- Administrators can inspect the academic period associated with a booking.
- Requests outside configured academic periods are identified as having no academic period association.
- When a coordinated booking spans different academic periods, the system identifies the applicable period for each resource occurrence.
- Academic period association does not replace the department and course information established in HIST-172 and HIST-173.
- Historical bookings retain their original association when future academic periods are created.

title: Bookings spanning academic period boundaries receive an incorrect period association.
description:
When a booking starts during one academic period and ends during another, the system may associate the entire booking with an incorrect academic period or fail to identify the boundary correctly. The expected behavior is to apply the documented academic period association rules consistently.
Reproduction steps:
1. Register two consecutive academic periods with different end and start dates.
2. Create a booking that begins on the final day of the first period and ends during the first day of the next period.
3. Submit the booking request.
4. Inspect the associated academic period in the booking details and reports.
Expected result: the booking follows the documented academic period assignment rule and is not silently associated with an unrelated period.
Actual result: the booking may receive an incorrect period association.
Acceptance criteria:
- Academic period boundaries are interpreted consistently using local calendar dates.
- The documented association rule is applied to bookings spanning two periods.
- The backend and reporting services use the same academic period calculation.
- Periods outside the requested date range are never assigned incorrectly.
- Automated tests cover bookings at the beginning, end and across academic period boundaries.

title: Implement API rate limiting and request protection.
description:
Implement request rate limiting and additional API protections in the Spring Boot backend to reduce the risk of automated abuse, excessive traffic and repeated unauthorized requests. Configure protection policies according to endpoint sensitivity while preserving the expected behavior of legitimate RoomBook users.
Acceptance criteria:
- Configurable request limits are implemented for selected API endpoint categories.
- Authentication-related endpoints receive appropriate protection against repeated requests.
- Publicly accessible endpoints and authenticated operations can have different rate limit policies.
- Rate limits can consider user identity and request source according to the security architecture.
- Requests exceeding configured limits receive an appropriate HTTP 429 response.
- Rate-limit responses include the necessary information for clients to handle temporary restrictions.
- Administrative configuration is maintained outside hardcoded application settings.
- Rate-limit events are recorded in operational monitoring without exposing credentials or sensitive data.
- Automated tests verify permitted requests, exceeded limits and recovery after the restriction window.

title: Configure exceptions to standard booking policies.
description:
As a RoomBook administrator, I want to define which booking policies can receive administrative exceptions, so that legitimate academic and institutional activities can be evaluated when they do not satisfy standard reservation rules.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized administrators can configure exception eligibility for specific booking policies.
- Exception rules can apply to selected resources, resource categories, campuses and institutional roles.
- Administrators can define which policy restrictions can be overridden through an exception.
- Each exception rule includes an active period and an explanatory description.
- The system prevents exceptions from bypassing mandatory security, authorization and resource integrity restrictions.
- Only authorized approvers can decide on eligible exception requests.
- Changes to exception rules are recorded in the audit history.
- The effective exception configuration is available during booking validation.

title: Request an exception to an applicable booking policy.
description:
As a university user, I want to request an exception when my booking does not satisfy an eligible reservation policy, so that an exceptional academic or institutional activity can be evaluated by the administrative office.
Acceptance criteria:
- When an eligible policy prevents a booking submission, the application identifies whether an exception request is permitted.
- The requester can submit an exception proposal with a written justification.
- The proposal identifies the resource, requested period and violated booking policy.
- The system verifies that the policy allows exceptions using the configuration established in HIST-212.
- Each proposal receives a unique identifier and Pending status.
- The original booking request is not approved or created as an approved reservation while the exception is pending.
- The requester can inspect the exception proposal and its current status.
- Exception submissions are recorded in the booking history or associated administrative history.
- Unauthorized users cannot request exceptions on behalf of other accounts without an explicit delegation permission.

title: Review and decide on booking policy exception requests.
description:
As a booking approver, I want to evaluate booking policy exception requests, so that I can authorize justified reservations that do not satisfy eligible standard booking restrictions.
Acceptance criteria:
- Approvers can access a dedicated queue of pending exception requests.
- Each entry displays the requester, resource, requested period and policy restriction involved.
- Approvers can inspect the justification and relevant booking information.
- The approver can approve or reject the exception with a recorded decision.
- Rejection requires a justification visible to the requester.
- Approval grants an exception only to the specific booking operation and policies identified in the proposal.
- The system revalidates current availability and all non-overridable restrictions before the booking can proceed.
- Decisions record the responsible approver, timestamp and justification when applicable.
- Requesters receive an update through RoomBook when a decision is registered.

title: Concurrent approval decisions create duplicate policy exceptions.
description:
When two approvers process the same pending policy exception simultaneously, the backend may register multiple decisions or create duplicate exception records. The expected behavior is to accept only one valid decision for the original proposal and preserve its complete administrative history.
Reproduction steps:
1. Submit a policy exception request.
2. Open the same request in two approver sessions.
3. Approve the request in the first session.
4. Attempt to approve or reject it in the second session using the previously opened page.
5. Inspect the exception records and booking history.
Expected result: the first successful decision is preserved, and the second operation is rejected because the proposal has already been processed.
Actual result: duplicate or conflicting decisions may be recorded.
Acceptance criteria:
- Exception decisions verify the current persisted proposal status.
- Only one decision can successfully transition a proposal out of Pending status.
- Repeated requests cannot create duplicate exception records.
- Unsuccessful attempts receive an explanatory response.
- Automated integration tests cover concurrent approval and rejection operations.

title: Configure post-booking feedback questionnaires.
description:
As a university administrator, I want to configure feedback questionnaires for completed bookings, so that RoomBook can collect structured information about resource conditions and the quality of university facilities.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized administrators can create and maintain feedback questionnaire templates.
- A questionnaire can contain rating questions, multiple-choice questions and optional written responses.
- Administrators can define which resource types or individual resources use each questionnaire.
- Questions can be marked as mandatory or optional.
- Administrators can define the period during which a requester can submit feedback after a completed booking.
- Active questionnaires are associated with eligible completed bookings.
- Changes to questionnaire templates do not modify feedback already submitted.
- Only users with the appropriate administration permission can modify questionnaire configurations.
- All questionnaire changes are recorded in the audit history.

title: Submit feedback after completing a university booking.
description:
As a university user, I want to submit feedback after using a room, laboratory or equipment item, so that the university can identify service issues and improve the quality of its resources.
Acceptance criteria:
- Eligible users can access the feedback questionnaire associated with their completed booking.
- The questionnaire displays the active questions configured in HIST-216.
- Mandatory questions must be answered before submission.
- Rating values are validated against the configured range.
- Written feedback follows the configured character limits.
- A submitted feedback record is associated with the original booking and resource.
- Users can submit feedback only for bookings belonging to their account and eligible attendance states.
- The system allows only one final feedback submission per booking and questionnaire unless an authorized correction is performed.
- The submission records the author and timestamp.
- The feedback confirmation is displayed after successful persistence.

title: Review submitted resource feedback.
description:
As a university administrator, I want to review feedback submitted by users about university resources, so that I can identify recurring problems and direct improvement activities to the appropriate departments.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized administrators can access a centralized feedback management interface.
- Each feedback entry displays the resource, questionnaire, submission date and answers.
- Administrators can filter feedback by campus, building, resource type, individual resource and reporting period.
- The interface distinguishes feedback requiring administrative attention from feedback that has been reviewed.
- Authorized administrators can add internal review notes without modifying the original user submission.
- Personally identifying information is displayed only to users with the appropriate permission.
- Feedback records remain linked to their original booking and resource.
- The interface supports pagination and sorting by submission date.
- All administrative review actions are recorded in the audit history.

title: Refreshing the feedback confirmation page creates duplicate submissions.
description:
After submitting feedback for a completed booking, refreshing the confirmation page or repeating the submission request may create multiple feedback records. The expected behavior is to preserve a single final submission for the same booking and questionnaire.
Reproduction steps:
1. Open an eligible completed booking.
2. Complete and submit its feedback questionnaire.
3. Wait for the confirmation page to appear.
4. Refresh the page or repeat the original submission request.
5. Inspect the feedback history for the booking.
Expected result: only one final feedback submission exists for that booking and questionnaire.
Actual result: duplicate feedback records may be created.
Acceptance criteria:
- Feedback submission enforces uniqueness for the booking and questionnaire combination.
- Repeated submissions of the same operation return a controlled response without creating another record.
- Database constraints prevent duplicate final submissions.
- Refreshing the confirmation page does not repeat the original write operation.
- Automated tests cover repeated submissions and concurrent requests.

title: Analyze user feedback trends across university resources.
description:
As a university administrator, I want to analyze feedback trends across campuses and resource categories, so that I can identify resources requiring corrective action and evaluate improvements over time.
Acceptance criteria:
- The reporting interface displays average ratings by resource, resource type, building and campus.
- Administrators can filter results by reporting period and questionnaire.
- The report includes submission counts and rating distributions.
- Results distinguish resources with no feedback from resources with low ratings.
- Administrators can identify recurring themes from available written responses through category filtering or keyword search.
- Feedback metrics are calculated from persisted questionnaire submissions.
- Reports preserve the privacy restrictions applied to individual feedback records.
- Results support pagination and export using the existing CSV and PDF reporting services.
- Only users with the appropriate reporting permission can access feedback analytics.

title: Configure mandatory safety instructions for equipment reservations.
description:
As a university equipment administrator, I want to register safety instructions and usage guidelines for equipment categories, so that users receive the necessary information before collecting and operating university devices.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized equipment administrators can create and maintain instruction documents or written guidelines.
- Instructions can be associated with one or more equipment categories or individual assets.
- Administrators can identify instructions that require mandatory acknowledgement.
- Each instruction has a version identifier, publication date and active status.
- Superseded instructions remain available in historical records.
- Mandatory instructions are presented to eligible requesters before equipment handover.
- Changes to published instructions are recorded in the audit history.
- Only authorized administrators can publish or deactivate safety instructions.

title: Acknowledge mandatory equipment usage instructions.
description:
As a requester, I want to review and acknowledge mandatory equipment safety instructions before collecting borrowed devices, so that I understand the operational requirements and responsibilities associated with their use.
Acceptance criteria:
- The equipment request detail page displays applicable instructions configured in HIST-221.
- Each mandatory instruction must be explicitly acknowledged before equipment handover.
- The acknowledgement records the authenticated requester, instruction identifier, instruction version and timestamp.
- Users can access previously acknowledged instruction versions through their request history.
- The system distinguishes mandatory acknowledgements from informational documents.
- Equipment managers can verify acknowledgement status during the handover operation.
- Updated mandatory instruction versions require a new acknowledgement when applicable.
- The acknowledgement does not replace other institutional authorization or safety procedures.
- Acknowledgement information is preserved as an auditable record.

title: Equipment handover proceeds without mandatory instruction acknowledgement.
description:
When an equipment request requires acknowledgement of safety instructions, the handover operation may still succeed if a user bypasses the frontend and calls the backend endpoint directly. The expected behavior is to enforce mandatory acknowledgement validation in the backend before recording equipment delivery.
Reproduction steps:
1. Configure a mandatory safety instruction for an equipment category.
2. Approve an equipment request for an item belonging to that category.
3. Do not acknowledge the displayed instruction.
4. Attempt to register equipment handover through the REST API.
5. Inspect the handover record.
Expected result: the handover operation is rejected because the required acknowledgement is missing.
Actual result: the backend may register the equipment delivery.
Acceptance criteria:
- The backend verifies every applicable mandatory acknowledgement before handover.
- Acknowledgements must correspond to the current applicable instruction version.
- Requests with missing acknowledgements cannot create delivery records.
- The frontend displays which instruction must be acknowledged before continuing.
- Automated security and integration tests cover direct API attempts and outdated acknowledgements.

title: Configure minimum inventory thresholds for equipment.
description:
As an equipment manager, I want to configure minimum inventory thresholds for equipment categories, so that the university can identify when available stock is approaching a level that requires replenishment or redistribution.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized equipment managers can configure a minimum available quantity for an equipment category.
- Thresholds must be non-negative integers.
- Different equipment categories can have independent thresholds.
- The system calculates available inventory using the current asset status and outstanding reservations.
- Reserved, delivered, damaged, under-maintenance, retired and disposed assets are treated according to the documented inventory availability rules.
- Managers can edit or deactivate existing threshold configurations.
- The effective threshold is displayed in the equipment inventory management interface.
- Changes to inventory thresholds are recorded in the audit history.

title: Notify equipment managers when inventory falls below its threshold.
description:
As an equipment manager, I want to receive notifications when available equipment inventory reaches or falls below its configured minimum threshold, so that I can take action before resource shortages affect university activities.
Acceptance criteria:
- The system evaluates inventory quantities against the thresholds configured in HIST-224.
- An alert is generated when the available quantity reaches or falls below the configured threshold.
- Notifications identify the equipment category, available quantity, configured threshold and associated campus when applicable.
- Alerts are delivered to the responsible equipment managers through the RoomBook notification center and configured e-mail service.
