- Repeated inventory evaluations do not create duplicate active alerts for an unchanged shortage condition.
- A new alert can be generated after inventory returns to an acceptable level and subsequently falls below the threshold again.
- Deactivated equipment categories do not generate new shortage alerts.
- Notification events use the existing transactional event processing mechanism.
- Delivery outcomes and alert creation timestamps are available to authorized administrators.

title: Delegate administrative approval permissions temporarily.
description:
As a booking approver, I want to delegate my approval permissions to another eligible university employee for a defined period, so that booking requests continue to be evaluated when I am unavailable.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized approvers can create temporary permission delegations.
- The delegation identifies the original approver and the substitute user.
- The substitute must have an eligible institutional account.
- The delegation requires a start timestamp and expiration timestamp.
- Administrators can restrict delegated permissions by campus and resource type.
- Delegated permissions cannot exceed the permissions held by the original approver.
- The system activates and expires delegations according to their configured validity period.
- Delegation creation, modification and revocation are recorded in the audit history.
- Users without permission to manage delegations cannot create delegations for other accounts.

title: View administrative actions performed under delegated permissions.
description:
As a RoomBook administrator, I want to distinguish actions performed by delegated approvers from actions performed by the original approvers, so that administrative decisions remain traceable and responsibilities are clearly identified.
Acceptance criteria:
- Administrative booking histories identify whether an action was performed using delegated permissions.
- Each delegated action records the authenticated user who performed it and the original approver who granted the delegation.
- The history displays the applicable delegation identifier and timestamp.
- Delegated approval and rejection decisions remain associated with the correct booking request.
- Administrators can filter audit records by original approver and delegated user.
- Delegated actions remain identifiable after the delegation expires or is revoked.
- The information is available only to users with appropriate administrative audit permissions.

title: Expired administrative delegations remain authorized.
description:
When a temporary approval delegation reaches its expiration timestamp, the backend may continue allowing the substitute user to perform administrative decisions using the previously granted permissions. The expected behavior is to revoke delegated permissions automatically when their validity period ends.
Reproduction steps:
1. Create a delegation between two eligible approvers with a defined expiration timestamp.
2. Sign in as the substitute approver.
3. Perform an approval operation before expiration.
4. Wait until the delegation expires.
5. Attempt another approval operation using the same authenticated session.
Expected result: the operation is rejected because the delegation has expired.
Actual result: the backend may continue accepting the delegated permission.
Acceptance criteria:
- Delegation expiration is checked during every authorization decision.
- Expired delegations cannot authorize new administrative operations.
- Existing authenticated sessions do not preserve expired delegated permissions.
- The frontend updates the available administrative actions after delegation expiration.
- Automated tests cover expiration boundaries and active sessions.

title: Configure response targets for booking approval requests.
description:
As a RoomBook administrator, I want to define expected response times for booking approval requests, so that the administrative office can establish service standards for evaluating reservations.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized administrators can configure approval response targets.
- Targets can vary by campus, resource type and booking urgency.
- Each target defines the maximum permitted time between request submission and the initial administrative decision.
- The configuration supports different working calendars and business hours.
- Requests awaiting additional information follow the configured pause or continuation policy.
- Administrators can define response targets independently for regular and exception requests.
- Changes to approval targets are recorded in the administrative audit history.
- Existing pending requests retain their historical target configuration unless explicitly recalculated by an authorized administrator.

title: Monitor booking approval deadlines.
description:
As a booking office coordinator, I want to monitor approval deadlines and overdue requests, so that I can identify administrative backlogs and prioritize requests requiring a decision.
Acceptance criteria:
- The administrative queue displays the applicable response deadline for each pending request.
- Requests approaching their deadline receive a visual indication.
- Requests exceeding their configured response target are identified as overdue.
- The interface distinguishes overdue requests from requests that are still within their response period.
- Coordinators can filter requests by deadline status, campus, resource type and assigned approver.
- The dashboard displays elapsed response time and remaining permitted time.
- Requests in Awaiting Information follow the configured deadline policy.
- Approved, rejected and cancelled requests are excluded from active deadline monitoring.
- The deadline information is calculated using the approval policies established in HIST-229.

title: Approval response deadlines are calculated incorrectly during weekends.
description:
When approval response targets use institutional working calendars, the system may count weekends or holidays as working periods. This can cause requests to appear overdue before their permitted response time has elapsed. The expected behavior is to calculate approval deadlines using the configured institutional calendar.
Reproduction steps:
1. Configure an approval response target based on university business hours.
2. Submit a booking request shortly before the end of Friday's working period.
3. Leave the request pending throughout the weekend.
4. Open the administrative queue on Monday.
5. Inspect the remaining response time.
Expected result: excluded weekend hours do not contribute to the elapsed response time.
Actual result: the request may appear overdue prematurely.
Acceptance criteria:
- Approval deadline calculations respect the configured working calendar.
- University holidays and excluded periods are considered.
- Paused requests follow the configured Awaiting Information policy.
- Calculations use consistent timestamp and time zone rules.
- Automated tests cover weekends, holidays and working-hour boundaries.

title: Implement scheduled monitoring of booking approval deadlines.
description:
Implement a scheduled backend process responsible for evaluating pending booking requests against their configured administrative response targets. The process must identify approaching and overdue deadlines and generate the corresponding administrative notifications using RoomBook's existing notification infrastructure.
Acceptance criteria:
- A configurable scheduled Spring Boot process evaluates pending booking requests.
- Deadline calculations use the configuration established in HIST-229.
- University working calendars and holiday exclusions are respected.
- Requests awaiting additional information follow their configured deadline policy.
- Approaching and overdue requests generate the corresponding notification events.
- Notifications are processed through the transactional event mechanism established in HIST-091.
- Repeated executions do not generate duplicate alerts for the same deadline condition.
- The process records execution status and processing timestamps.
- Failed processing can be retried without losing pending notification events.
- Operational logs provide sufficient information for troubleshooting.

title: Search historical administrative audit events.
description:
As a university auditor, I want to search administrative audit events using filters and keywords, so that I can investigate specific operations and reconstruct the sequence of actions performed within RoomBook.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized auditors can access a centralized audit search interface.
- Search criteria include responsible user, action category, affected entity and date range.
- Users can search using entity identifiers and institutional user identifiers.
- Multiple search criteria can be combined.
- Results display the action type, responsible user, affected entity and timestamp.
- Selecting an entry opens its available audit details.
- Search results respect the auditor's campus and administrative access permissions.
- The interface supports sorting and pagination.
- Historical audit records are retrieved without allowing modification of their original contents.

title: Export filtered administrative audit records.
description:
As a university auditor, I want to export filtered administrative audit records, so that I can preserve evidence of relevant operations and perform external compliance reviews.
Acceptance criteria:
- The audit search interface provides a CSV export option.
- The export includes all records matching the selected filters rather than only the currently displayed page.
- Exported fields include event identifier, timestamp, responsible user, action category, affected entity and available event details.
- The export includes the reporting period and applied filters.
- Sensitive credentials, authentication tokens and restricted personal information are excluded.
- CSV values are properly escaped.
- Generated files use descriptive filenames containing the export date.
- Only authorized auditors can generate and download audit exports.
- Export operations are themselves recorded in the audit history.

title: Audit searches omit events when multiple filters are combined.
description:
When an auditor combines filters in the administrative audit search, the backend may return incomplete results because some filter conditions are incorrectly applied or ignored. The expected behavior is to return every event matching all selected conditions.
Reproduction steps:
1. Open the administrative audit search interface.
2. Select a responsible user and an action category.
3. Define a reporting date range.
4. Execute the search.
5. Compare the results with the corresponding persisted audit records.
Expected result: every returned record matches the selected user, action category and date range.
Actual result: matching events may be omitted or unrelated events may appear.
Acceptance criteria:
- All active filters are applied consistently by the backend.
- Combined filters use the documented logical conditions.
- Pagination and total record counts reflect the complete filtered dataset.
- CSV exports use the same filtering logic as the search interface.
- Automated integration tests cover individual and combined filter conditions.

title: Optimize database queries for administrative audit searches.
description:
Review PostgreSQL queries used by audit search and export operations. Implement appropriate indexes and query improvements to support searches across responsible users, action categories, affected entities and reporting periods while preserving the immutability of historical audit records.
Acceptance criteria:
- Existing audit search queries are analyzed using PostgreSQL execution plans.
- Indexes are created for frequently filtered and sorted audit fields where justified by query analysis.
- Search optimizations preserve the original event information and ordering requirements.
- Database changes are implemented through version-controlled migrations.
- Audit exports continue returning the complete matching dataset.
- Index migrations can be executed in development, testing and production environments.
- Automated tests verify search and export results after the changes.
- The indexing strategy is documented for future maintenance.

title: Request an export of personal RoomBook information.
description:
As a university user, I want to request an export of the personal information associated with my RoomBook account, so that I can review the information maintained by the application.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authenticated users can request an export of their personal RoomBook information.
- The export includes available profile information, personal preferences, booking records, notification preferences and personal activity records according to the data access policy.
- Information belonging exclusively to other users is excluded.
- Internal administrative notes and restricted institutional information are excluded from ordinary personal exports.
- The system creates a uniquely identified export request with a processing status.
- Users can inspect the status of their export requests.
- Completed exports are made available through an authenticated and time-limited download mechanism.
- Export generation uses the user's current authorization context.
- Requests and downloads are recorded in the audit history.

title: Review and process personal information access requests.
description:
As a university privacy administrator, I want to manage personal information access requests, so that I can verify and respond to requests submitted by university users through RoomBook.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized privacy administrators can access a centralized queue of personal information requests.
- Each request displays its identifier, requester, submission date and processing status.
- Administrators can inspect the data categories requested by the user.
- The workflow supports Pending, In Review, Completed and Rejected statuses.
- Rejected requests require an administrative justification.
- Administrators can inspect the corresponding export generated in HIST-237.
- Requests must be completed or rejected by an authorized privacy administrator.
- Each processing action records the responsible user, timestamp and justification when applicable.
- Requesters can view the current status of their own requests.

title: Submit a request to correct personal profile information.
description:
As a university user, I want to request correction of inaccurate personal information maintained by RoomBook, so that my institutional profile and associated booking records reflect the appropriate information.
Acceptance criteria:
- Users can submit a personal information correction request through their profile.
- The request identifies the information requiring correction and provides the proposed value or explanation.
- The requester must provide a justification for the correction.
- The system creates a uniquely identified request with Pending status.
- Authorized privacy administrators can review the requested correction.
- Information originating from the university SSO cannot be directly overwritten when the university identity provider remains its authoritative source.
- Accepted corrections are applied through the appropriate authorized data update process.
- Rejected corrections include an explanatory justification.
- The original and corrected information are traceable through the applicable audit records.

title: Personal data exports include other users' booking information.
description:
When a user requests an export of their personal information, the export generation process may include booking records or notification information belonging to other university accounts due to an incorrect association query. The expected behavior is to restrict every exported record to the authenticated requester's own information, subject to the configured data access policy.
Reproduction steps:
1. Create booking records for two different university users.
2. Sign in as the first user.
3. Request a personal information export through HIST-237.
4. Download and inspect the generated file.
Expected result: the export contains only records belonging to the authenticated requester and permitted associated information.
Actual result: records associated with another user may appear.
Acceptance criteria:
- Export queries enforce authenticated user ownership at the backend.
- Related records are included only when their association is authorized.
- Internal administrative information is excluded from ordinary personal exports.
- Export downloads enforce ownership independently of the original request page.
- Automated security tests cover records belonging to multiple users.

title: Configure retention policies for historical RoomBook information.
description:
As a university administrator, I want to configure retention policies for application records and attachments, so that RoomBook preserves institutional information according to university requirements and applies consistent rules to data that has reached the end of its retention period.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized administrators can configure retention rules for supported data categories.
- Retention categories include expired notifications, obsolete attachments, completed booking records and operational records where applicable.
- Each rule defines a retention duration and the resulting treatment after expiration.
- Supported treatments distinguish permanent preservation, archival and deletion where institutionally authorized.
- Active bookings and records subject to an active administrative or legal retention hold are excluded from automatic deletion.
- Retention rules cannot override mandatory institutional preservation requirements.
- Changes to retention policies are recorded in the audit history.
- The system displays the effective policy associated with each supported data category.

title: Review records scheduled for archival or deletion.
description:
As a university records administrator, I want to review records that have reached their configured retention period, so that I can verify whether they are eligible for archival or deletion before the corresponding operation is performed.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized records administrators can access a retention review interface.
- The interface displays eligible records grouped by data category and configured retention rule.
- Each entry identifies the record, original creation date, retention expiration date and proposed treatment.
- Records under an active retention hold are clearly identified and excluded from standard processing.
- Administrators can inspect the associated institutional record before approving its treatment.
- The system supports filtering by category, retention rule and expiration period.
- Review decisions require an authorized administrative user.
- Approval and rejection actions are recorded in the audit history.
- Records remain unchanged until the required retention operation is authorized.

title: Implement automated retention policy processing.
description:
Implement a scheduled backend process responsible for evaluating approved retention policies and processing records authorized for archival or deletion. The mechanism must respect active retention holds, preserve required institutional audit information and maintain traceability for every operation.
Acceptance criteria:
- A scheduled Spring Boot process evaluates active retention policies established in HIST-241.
- Only records eligible under the configured policy and approved through the review workflow are processed when approval is required.
- Active retention holds prevent automatic archival or deletion.
- Archival and deletion operations are executed according to the configured treatment.
- The process records affected record identifiers, policy references, responsible authorization and execution timestamps.
- Repeated executions do not process the same approved operation more than once.
- Failures are recorded and can be investigated by authorized administrators.
- The process does not delete immutable audit records or mandatory historical records.
- Database and object storage operations maintain consistent metadata.
- Automated tests cover retention eligibility, holds, retries and completed operations.

title: Submit a technical support request through RoomBook.
description:
As a university user, I want to submit a technical support request when I encounter a problem using RoomBook, so that the application support team can investigate issues that are unrelated to resource maintenance.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authenticated users can submit a technical support request through the application.
- The request requires a subject, description and support category.
- Supported categories include login problems, booking errors, catalog issues, notification problems and general application usage.
- The requester can optionally attach screenshots or supporting documents using the existing object storage integration.
- Each support request receives a unique identifier and an initial Open status.
- The system automatically associates the request with the authenticated user.
- Submission confirmation displays the support request identifier.
- Technical support requests are stored separately from maintenance incident reports.
- Submitted requests are accessible to authorized support personnel.

title: Track the progress of technical support requests.
description:
As a university user, I want to track the status of my technical support requests, so that I can understand whether my reported application problem is being investigated or resolved.
Acceptance criteria:
- Users can view support requests submitted through their own accounts.
- Each request displays its identifier, subject, category, current status and latest update timestamp.
- Supported statuses include Open, Assigned, In Progress, Awaiting User Response, Resolved and Closed.
- Authorized support personnel can update the request status and add progress comments.
- Comments can be classified as internal or visible to the requester.
- Users can respond when additional information is requested.
- Status changes and requester responses are recorded chronologically.
- Requesters receive notifications when their support request status changes.
- Users cannot access support requests submitted by other accounts.

title: Technical support requests are accessible to unauthorized users.
description:
When a user accesses a support request using a previously obtained request identifier, the API may return information belonging to another requester without verifying ownership or support permissions. The expected behavior is to restrict support request access to its owner and explicitly authorized support personnel.
Reproduction steps:
1. Sign in as User A and submit a technical support request.
2. Obtain the support request identifier.
3. Sign in as User B using a different university account.
4. Attempt to access User A's support request through the REST API and frontend URL.
Expected result: access is rejected because User B does not own the request and does not have support permissions.
Actual result: request information may be returned to User B.
Acceptance criteria:
- The backend verifies request ownership or explicit support authorization for every access operation.
- Guessing or obtaining another request identifier does not grant access.
- Attachment downloads apply the same authorization checks.
- Internal comments are restricted to authorized support personnel.
- Automated security tests cover direct API access and unauthorized attachment retrieval.

title: Provide contextual onboarding guides for RoomBook users.
description:
As a first-time RoomBook user, I want to access onboarding instructions relevant to my institutional role, so that I can understand how to use the application and complete common tasks independently.
Acceptance criteria:
- The application provides an onboarding section accessible from the main navigation.
- Guides are available for students, professors, university staff, booking approvers and resource managers.
- Each guide explains the main workflows associated with its intended role.
- Instructions include relevant navigation references and application screenshots where available.
- Users can search guides by keyword and category.
- Guide content is maintained by authorized administrators through the configured documentation management process.
- Guides can be updated without requiring a frontend deployment.
- Users can access publicly available onboarding information without exposing restricted administrative procedures.
- Guide content follows the established accessibility guidelines.

title: Require acknowledgement of updated institutional usage policies.
description:
As a RoomBook user, I want to review and acknowledge applicable institutional usage policies, so that I understand the conditions governing the use of university resources and the RoomBook platform.
Acceptance criteria:
- Authorized administrators can publish usage policies with a unique version identifier and effective date.
- The application identifies users who have not acknowledged the currently applicable mandatory policy version.
- Users must review and acknowledge mandatory policies before performing the operations restricted by the policy configuration.
- The system records the user, policy version and acknowledgement timestamp.
- Updated policy versions can require a new acknowledgement.
- Previously acknowledged versions remain available in the user's acknowledgement history.
- Users cannot acknowledge policies on behalf of another account without explicit authorization.
- Policy publication and modification events are recorded in the administrative audit history.
- The acknowledgement workflow supports the university's applicable accessibility requirements.

title: Previously acknowledged policies are incorrectly treated as current after an update.
description:
When an administrator publishes a new version of an institutional usage policy, RoomBook may continue considering users compliant based on their acknowledgement of an earlier version. The expected behavior is to require acknowledgement of the currently applicable mandatory version whenever the policy configuration demands it.
Reproduction steps:
1. Publish and activate policy version 1.
2. Sign in as a university user and acknowledge version 1.
3. Publish version 2 and mark it as requiring renewed acknowledgement.
4. Return to RoomBook using the original user's authenticated account.
5. Attempt to perform an operation restricted until the updated policy is acknowledged.
Expected result: the application requests acknowledgement of version 2 before allowing the restricted operation.
Actual result: the system may consider the acknowledgement of version 1 sufficient.
Acceptance criteria:
- Policy acknowledgement checks compare the user's record with the currently applicable policy version.
- Publishing a new mandatory version updates the acknowledgement requirements.
- Older acknowledgement records remain preserved.
- Restricted operations are validated by the backend.
- Automated tests cover new versions, existing acknowledgements and policy-specific exceptions.

title: Establish production release validation and end-to-end acceptance tests.
description:
Implement the final release validation process for RoomBook, combining automated end-to-end tests, integration verification and production deployment checks. The objective is to ensure that the complete booking lifecycle and supporting administrative operations work together correctly before each approved production release.
Acceptance criteria:
- Automated end-to-end tests cover university SSO authentication and logout.
- Tests cover resource discovery, availability searches and booking request submission.
- Tests cover administrative approval, rejection, modification and cancellation workflows.
- Tests cover maintenance blocks, equipment handover, return operations and inventory updates.
- Tests cover notification generation and delivery processing using the configured test environment.
- Tests cover reporting, CSV and PDF exports, and administrative audit access.
- Tests cover role-based authorization and unauthorized access scenarios.
- Tests validate the integration between the React frontend, Spring Boot API and PostgreSQL database.
- The CI/CD pipeline executes the required validation suite before production deployment.
- Production deployment requires successful health checks and the configured release approval.
- Release validation results are stored with the corresponding application version.
- A failed release validation prevents the production deployment from proceeding.
